items.readme:
# Agent Autoloop **让你的命令行 Agent 在后台自己接活、自己跟进到底；平时不烦你，遇到拿不准的事才发卡片找你拍板。** **中文** | [English](README.en.md) [上手](#上手) · [场景模板](#拿来即用的场景模板) · [插件](#插件体系四个方向都能自由替换) · [内核](#内核的四个机制) · [文档](#更多文档) ![架构图](docs/architecture.svg) ## 它解决什么问题？ 平时我们用 Claude Code、Codex 这类命令行 Agent，大多是“人守着终端用”：你输一句话，盯着它跑，等它问你下一步；一旦关掉窗口或者人走开，事情就断了。 **Agent Autoloop** 是一个极轻量的自动化中台。它把任务调度做成一个零外部依赖的**内核**，把事件来源、Agent、通知通道，甚至代码上线流水线全部拆成可随时插拔的**插件**。 - **一台电脑、一条命令就能跑。** 装在你的 Windows、Mac 或 Linux 上，不用买云服务器，也不用开放公网端口。 - **一行配置接新 Agent。** 不需要 SDK，也不需要改 Agent 源码，能接收提示词并打印最后一条回复的命令行工具都能接。 - **没有后台界面。** 需要你拍板时把卡片推到飞书、钉钉、企微、Slack、Discord 或桌面通知；想看全局进展，敲一行命令。 ## 上手 支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。需要 Node 24 或更新、Git，以及一个已经登录的命令行 Agent；macOS/Linux 还需要 curl，不需要 GitHub 账号。也可以把[安装说明](INSTALL.md)交给你的 Agent。 Windows PowerShell： ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` macOS / Linux： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop/main/install.sh | sh ``` 安装和 `agent-autoloop update` 都装最新的 [Release](https://github.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop/releases)，那是通过了全部检查的版本。 装好后用你本机的 Agent 真实走一遍“提问 → 退出等回复 → 拍板 → 接着干完”： ```bash agent-autoloop try ``` 下面是在终端里的真实输出： ```text 事件发出去了，Agent 开始干活…… Agent 结束了这一轮，问了你一个问题。它现在不占进程、不花 Token。 【等你决定】#1 试跑：选一个颜色 这是一次试跑，选哪个都行。 1. 蓝色 2. 绿色 回答：agent-autoloop answer 1 <序号> 答完运行 agent-autoloop status，能看到它接着把活干完。 ``` 交互终端里直接输入数字回车；非交互终端运行 `agent-autoloop answer 1 2` 选择“绿色”。再跑 `agent-autoloop status`，就能看到它接上刚才的会话并显示“你选了绿色，试跑通过”，还有今天和最近 7 天的轮数、Token 和费用（[统计口径](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#看情况回答)）。 ## 一件事怎么转起来 编号和上面的架构图一一对应： 1. **新事件进来。** 早上 9 点的定时任务、GitHub 上新提的 Issue、业务系统报的错，都变成一条标准事件送进内核。 2. **按规则派活。** 内核照你写的规则，决定交给哪个 Agent、去哪个目录干。同一件事排队时又来的消息，会合并成一轮处理。 3. **干完一轮就退出。** Agent 把结果写在最后一条回复里，进程直接退出。 4. **拿不准才问你。** 碰到删数据、重启服务、花钱、对外发消息这类事，内核通过飞书或桌面通知发一张卡片给你。等你回复期间，它不占后台进程，也不消耗 Token。 5. **点一下，接着干。** 你选完，它接上原来的对话，把剩下的活干完。 能自己搞定的事走图上方的自动闭环：直接办完，或者约个时间（比如半小时后）再醒来复查，全程不打扰你。 ## 日常怎么配？ ### 写一份规则（`rules.json`） 不需要写胶水代码。打开 `~/.agent-autoloop/rules.json`，在 `rules` 里写清楚**什么事、交给谁、在哪个目录干**。`to` 填 `agents` 里已有的名字。比如每天早上 9 点写早报： ```json { "name": "早报", "when": { "cron": "0 9 * * *" }, "to": "codex", "cwd": "~/notes", "prompt": "整理昨天的笔记和提交，写今天的早报。" } ``` 外部事件写法一样，只是要先接好来源。比如有人提新 Issue 时交给 Codex，先按[说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个事件插件)在 `sources` 里登记 `github`： ```json { "name": "处理 issue", "when": { "source": "github", "types": ["issues.opened"] }, "to": "codex", "cwd": "~/code/app", "skill": "handle-issue", "parallel": 3 } ``` `agent-autoloop pause <规则>`、`resume <规则>` 暂停和恢复一条规则，暂停期间到点不跑、来事件不接，恢复后不补跑；`agent-autoloop run <规则>` 立即跑一轮。这些记在中台的日志里，不改 `rules.json`。 保存后几秒内自动生效，可以运行 `agent-autoloop check` 检查，`agent-autoloop check <文件>` 检查一份草稿，不碰正在跑的中台；`agent-autoloop rules explain [文件]` 看生效的规则和下次定时（也可以指定一份草稿），`agent-autoloop emit <类型> --dry-run` 预演一条事件会派给谁（不连接中台、不写日志）。就算改错了，或者文件被删、读不到，系统也会继续按旧规则跑，并发卡片提醒你。 ### Agent 怎么跟中台配合？ 中台对 Agent 只有一个约定：**在最后一条回复里交代结果**。事情办完了，正常输出一句结论就行。需要向你请示时，在回复末尾附一段 `agent-autoloop` 代码块： ````text 订单已经核对完毕，库存充足。 ```agent-autoloop { "ask": [{ "title": "怎么发货？", "text": "两种方式今天都能发出。", "options": ["快递", "自提"], "key": "shipping" }] } ``` ```` 除了提问（`ask`），还能发通知（`notice`）、关闭已解决的卡片（`resolve`）、预约复查（`later`）和触发新事件（`events`）。通告不需要回答，但结案时可以顺手写一句处理说明，这句话会留在卡片上；只是告诉一声的通告标成 `fyi`，不带按钮。万一 JSON 写错了，中台只让它在原会话里重写最后这段回复，不会把已经干完的业务重做一遍；重写也失败时，保留原结论并通知你回执没有生效（通用命令没有会话，直接走这一步）。接着旧会话跑也一样：会话接不上才开新的；接上了、干到一半断了，就算没跑成，过几分钟回到原会话重试，不开新会话重做。同一事项的新事件默认开新会话；规则写 `"resume": true` 就接着上一轮的会话。 ## 拿来即用的场景模板 每套模板都带规则、任务 Skill 和启用说明。 | 想做什么 | 已经封装好的流程 | |---|---| | [每日早报](examples/recipes/morning-brief/README.md) | 默认每天 8 点整理本地笔记和 Git 提交，写入 `briefs/YYYY-MM-DD.md` | | [跟进 GitHub Issue](examples/recipes/github-issues/README.md) | 每 5 分钟查新 Issue，在本地改代码并通知你查看；不提交、不推送、不回复 Issue | | [线上告警排查](examples/recipes/ops-alerts/README.md) | 接收报错、对照代码查原因，需要重启时发卡片询问，回答后继续 | | [用户反馈处理](examples/recipes/feedback/README.md) | 重读反馈当前状态、修复、交付核实、准备回复；需要决定时飞书问你，回答后继续 | | [网站巡检](examples/recipes/website-watch/README.md) | 每 5 分钟检查状态和关键内容，首次异常交给 Agent，持续异常不重复通知，恢复后更新原卡片 | | [飞书周报与业务摘要](examples/recipes/feishu-brief/README.md) | 周日 18 点按你的权限读汇报和指定表格，生成本地摘要；飞书只发简短摘要，完整稿留在本机 | | [收件箱分诊](examples/recipes/inbox-triage/README.md) | 默认每天 8 点读过去 24 小时的未读邮件，写成清单和回复草稿；不发送、不改邮箱状态 | | [PR 自动交付](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#交付流水线) | 打上 `deliver` 标签后，审查、等 CI、合并、等发布并核对线上版本 | **启用：** 打开对应说明，把任务 Skill 放进所用 Agent 的 skills 目录，把示例规则合入 `~/.agent-autoloop/rules.json`，替换电脑名和路径，再运行 `agent-autoloop check`。 反馈处理、网站巡检、飞书摘要和收件箱分诊默认使用北京时间，只发给本人的飞书私聊。样例数据都是虚构的；脚本和回执只用本地 HTTP 与假飞书 CLI 验证过，没有在真实账号上跑过完整业务。 更多模板：[Claude 委托 Codex 处理网页](examples/recipes/browser-handoff/README.md)、[每周代码清理](examples/skills/weekly-sweep/SKILL.md)、[交付 PR](examples/skills/ship-pr/SKILL.md)。 ## 插件体系：四个方向都能自由替换 内置插件随程序安装，填好配置即可启用；第三方插件用 `agent-autoloop add ` 安装。 | 方向 | 内置 | 配置 | |---|---|---| | **事件**：怎么发现新活 | [GitHub Webhook](plugins/github/source.ts)、[GitLab Webhook](plugins/gitlab/source.ts)、[HTTP 接口](docs/protocol.md#来源把世界变成事件)、[定时规则](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#改规则)、[Issue 轮询脚本](examples/watch-github-issues.sh) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个事件插件) | | **Agent**：谁来干活 | [Claude Code](plugins/claude/agent.ts)、[Codex](plugins/codex/agent.ts)、[ACP](plugins/acp/agent.ts)、[DeepSeek Harness](plugins/dsh/agent.ts)、[通用命令](plugins/command/agent.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个-agent) | | **通道**：去哪找你拍板 | [桌面通知](plugins/desktop/channel.ts)（默认开启）、[飞书](plugins/feishu/channel.ts)、[钉钉 / 企微 / Slack / Discord](plugins/webhook/templates.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个通道) | | **交付**：把 CI/CD 也做成插件 | [`delivery`](plugins/delivery/delivery.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#交付流水线) | **实测情况：** Claude Code、Codex 和 ACP（官方 Codex ACP 适配器）跑通了多轮问答和跨进程会话续接；飞书跑通了发送、按钮回调和卡片更新；四种 Webhook 模板只在本地模拟服务上验证过，GitLab Webhook 按官方文档的格式测试，没连过真实 GitLab。这些文字通道靠回答链接拍板，要把 `hub.publicUrl` 配成手机或电脑能打开的地址。 **内置 Agent 走第三方网关。** Claude Code、Codex 要接第三方模型服务，或者启动前要先设好环境变量，写一个设好变量再启动它的小脚本，在 Agent 里写 `"program": "脚本路径"`，会话续接和用量统计照旧，见[说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个-agent)。 **其他命令行 Agent 一行接入。** 设置 `use: "command"` 并传入命令数组，`{prompt}` 作为独立参数传递，不会被当成 shell 代码执行。下面的命令整理自各家官方文档，我们还没有逐个跑过： | Agent | 接入命令 | |---|---| | [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/cli-help.md#dsh-headless) 旧版（内置插件要 0.2.2 或更新） | `dsh --profile headless {prompt}` | | [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md) | `pi --print {prompt}` | | [OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/agent) | `openclaw agent exec {prompt}` | | [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/cli) | `hermes chat -Q -q {prompt}` | | [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/parameters) | `agent -p --trust {prompt}` | | [WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy](https://www.codebuddy.ai/docs/cli/headless) | `codebuddy -p {prompt}` | OpenClaw 的 `agent exec` 每次默认最多跑 600 秒，到点就算失败；要跑更久的，在命令里加 `--timeout <秒>`（`0` 不限时）。 会说 ACP 的 Agent 用 `use: "acp"` 接，还能接着原来的会话做：[Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/acp-mode/) 写 `"command": ["gemini", "--acp"]`，[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/docs/acp) 写 `"command": ["opencode", "acp"]`。这两条已经跑通了 ACP 握手（Gemini CLI 0.67.0、OpenCode 1.1.2），多轮问答和会话续接还没跑过。 **交付流水线。** 给 GitHub PR 打上 `deliver` 标签后，它会自己跟进到上线：**审代码 → 等 CI → 合并 PR → 等部署 → 核对线上版本**。审查和交付配置只从 `main` 读取，绝不在接单电脑上检出或运行 PR 里的代码；排队、并发和重试直接复用内核。 **写自己的插件。** 从 [Agent](examples/plugins/hello-agent/agent.ts)、[通道](examples/plugins/hello-channel/channel.ts)、[事件](examples/plugins/hello-source/source.ts) 三个可运行的最小模板开始，见[插件开发说明](docs/plugins.md)。要让 Agent 操作网页，先看[浏览器接入](docs/plugins.md#浏览器接入)。命令行和 [MCP](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#mcp-与密钥撤销) 也能查看和回答卡片。 ## 内核的四个机制 内核约 1850 行代码、零运行时依赖。它不读系统时钟、不用随机数、不向外发请求，插件主动连进来，账号凭据留在各自的插件里；同样的输入永远得出同样的结果。它把四个计算机领域的成熟做法用到了命令行 Agent 上： - **挂起零消耗**：等你拍板时进程直接退出，等待状态存在数据库里，Agent 不用一直挂着。你三天没回，这三天就没有 Agent 进程在跑、不花 Token，只有很轻的中台在后台等着；你一回答，它接着原来的对话继续干。 - **事件溯源**：所有状态都从一条只追加的日志算出来，日志和索引在同一个事务里写进磁盘，写完才应答。进程被强杀，已经确认的事不丢（整机断电没有单独测过）；任何一轮为什么跑、结果是什么，一条命令就能查清；数据格式变了就从日志重建，不用写迁移脚本。 - **指令数据分离**：思路和 SQL 参数化一样。Issue 的标题和正文等外部文字只作为资料放进文件，不拼进提示词，提示词里只有校验过字符的类型、编号和链接；用哪个 Agent、在哪个目录、什么权限，只由你本机的规则决定，事件里带 `cwd`、`agent`、`access` 字段会被直接拒收。 - **跳数熔断**：思路和网络包的 TTL 一样。Agent 交回的事件会再派给 Agent，层数一路累加，经过人工提问和定时复查也不清零，Agent 自己改不了；超过 8 层就只记录、不再派活，并发一张卡片告诉你。 ### 自己跑一遍 Windows 用 `npm run test:windows` 和 `node scripts/install-smoke-windows.ts`，运行共用行为测试与原生进程、安装检查；Unix shell 测试仍在 Linux/macOS 上跑。 在程序目录 `~/.agent-autoloop/app` 下运行： | 验证什么 | 命令 | |---|---| | 任何一轮的来龙去脉 | `agent-autoloop why 1` | | 20 万步模拟断网、丢包、崩溃和重复提交，一个种子就能复现 | `node sim/random.ts 24301 200000` | | 强杀进程 1000 次，已确认的记录一条不丢 | `node sim/crash.ts 1000 12648430` | | 下面的性能数字 | `npm run benchmark` | ```text 第 1 轮 · 演示 11-03 20:47:25 规则版本 #1 11-03 20:47:25 触发事件：来源 local · 类型 demo.start · 对象 example 11-03 20:47:25 local 领取（演示程序） 11-03 20:47:25 结束：演示完成 ``` ### 实测性能 Apple M5 Pro、24 GB、Node 24.21.0。写入逐条提交，事务落盘后才应答。 | 指标 | 实测 | |---|---:| | 冷启动 | 88.78 ms | | 空闲内存 | 59.94 MB RSS | | 1000 个同时等待的长轮询 | 170.49 MB RSS | | 持久化写入 | 2394 条/秒 | | 派活 p99 | 1.82 ms | | 排队 5000 时被挡下的心跳 p99 | 1.66 ms | | 110 万条事实时的启动 | 99.8 ms | | 内核行数（含空行和注释） | 约 1850 | | 运行时依赖 | 0 | 历史变大后，状态汇总会变慢，日志和索引也继续占磁盘；格式变化后的首次启动要从日志全量重建，110 万条用时 43.1 秒。[完整数据和测法](docs/protocol.md#历史增长实测)。 ## 用量与合规说明 中台直接调用你本机已经安装并登录好的命令行工具，不会读取或转存你的账号凭据。模型调用消耗算在你自己的账号名下，额度和使用范围遵循各家模型厂商的服务条款。 在高频自动化场景下，各家厂商通常更建议使用 API Key（个人订阅额度主要是为日常人工交互设计的，详见 [Anthropic](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) 与 [OpenAI](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth) 的官方说明）。如果你用它对外提供服务，请使用 API Key。本项目为独立开源项目，与上述厂商无隶属或背书关系。 ## 更多文档 - [安装说明](INSTALL.md) - [规则与交付流水线配置手册](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md) - [如何编写插件](docs/plugins.md) - [完整通信协议](docs/protocol.md) - [安全边界说明](SECURITY.md) - [参与贡献与交流](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [项目开发约定](AGENTS.md)
仓库目录 | 位置 | 放什么 | |---|---| | `kernel/` | 内核：决策、事实日志、状态投影、到期任务、规则匹配、接口行为与卡片表单 | | `host/` | 运行外壳：Node HTTP、文件与 SQLite 连接、时钟、配置、状态汇总、后台服务和插件加载 | | `protocol/` | 通信格式、JSON Schema、输入校验、HTTP 客户端和一致性检查 | | `worker/` | 接单程序：领活、运行 Agent、心跳与停止、读取和提交回执 | | `cli/`、`bin/` | 用户命令及启动入口，包括状态、回答、`why`、MCP、更新与卸载 | | `plugins/` | 内置 Agent、事件、通道和交付插件 | | `examples/recipes/` | 完整场景：规则、任务 Skill 和启用说明 | | `examples/plugins/`、`examples/skills/`、`examples/*.sh` | 最小插件模板、独立任务手册和 Shell 示例 | | `skills/agent-autoloop/` | 中台的正式配置与操作手册，安装时也提供给 Agent 使用 | | `docs/` | 通信协议、插件开发说明与中英文架构图 | | `tests/`、`sim/` | 日常行为测试，以及模拟、穷举、强杀和变异检查 | | `scripts/`、`.github/workflows/` | 性能与真机验证、安装冒烟脚本，以及 Windows / Linux / macOS CI | | 根目录文档与 `install.sh` | 中英文 README、安装说明、安全边界、开发约定、许可证与安装脚本 | 读代码可以从 `bin/agent-autoloop.ts` → `cli/main.ts` 开始，再按功能进入 `host/`、`worker/` 或 `plugins/`；内核设计先看[协议](docs/protocol.md)。同名文件分属不同层：`host/http.ts` 转换 Node 请求，`kernel/http.ts` 定义接口行为；`protocol/rules.ts` 校验输入，`kernel/rules.ts` 定义规则类型和匹配。

items.readme:
*关于本项目：HGhub 只是我体验 Tuari2 移动端开发时做的小玩具，开源几天后不知为何收到了大量star。* *意识到可能存在的潜在危险后，我立刻更换了开源协议为 **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** ，并在 Readme 中写入了大量保护自己的文段。目前 HGhub收到的star实际上德不配位。* *在之后的更新中，我不再会维护任何获取上游数据的工作，维护方向将偏重于 UI/UX 与使用体验，同时仍会低频率的响应 PR 与 Issues。如果版权方或其授权代表认为本项目涉及其合法权益，欢迎通过 GitHub 仓库留言联系。收到明确的权利方通知后，我会第一时间积极响应，并根据对方诉求立即归档项目或将仓库转为私有，停止公开访问。*
# HGhub **黄果短剧第三方客户端 · Rust + Tauri 2** Windows / macOS / Android 三端 · Fluent 设计 · 沉浸式竖屏播放
> ⚠️ 本项目仅供 **学习与技术交流**，不提供、不存储、不分发任何音视频内容。 > 所有内容均来自第三方站点，版权归原作者与上游站点所有。 **使用须知** - **以访客身份正常使用**：像普通访客一样浏览就好，请勿滥用本项目。 - **不要给上游增加压力**：本项目本身不提供下载功能，请勿改动代码去做批量下载 / 批量抓取，也不要高频轮询、并发轰炸接口或挂机刷播放量；内置的封面与播放列表缓存请不要改小或关掉。 - **尊重上游版权**：不要去除水印与站点标识，不要把剧集搬运、转码、修改后二次分发到别处（网盘、资源站、其他 App 等），更不能改完拿出去出售。 - **不要公开传播接口与直链**：接口地址、播放直链、解密方式请勿公开张贴或打包成「资源站」——上游一旦封禁，所有人都没法再用。 - **不要商业化**：禁止打包出售、接入广告 / 会员 / 付费点播，或作为收费服务的一部分分发（详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)）。 - **合理使用**：仅供个人学习、研究与自用；请在 24 小时内删除相关资源，并支持正版。 - **遵守当地法律**：使用者应自行判断并承担合规责任。 > ⚖️ 许可证自 v1.1.0 版本起改为 **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0**：**禁止任何商业用途**—— > 包括打包出售、接入付费/会员/广告变现、作为收费产品或服务的一部分分发。 > 个人学习、研究、自用与非营利使用不受限制，详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。 ## 官方渠道与仿冒提醒 - **唯一官方仓库**：[github.com/Minireel/HGhub](https://github.com/Minireel/HGhub) - **唯一下载渠道**：[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Minireel/HGhub/releases)。仓库源码页不放任何可执行文件， 其余网站、网盘、QQ 群、公众号、第三方下载站分发的「HGhub」安装包**一律非官方**，作者不保证其安全性与完整性。 > 🚫 **已发现的恶意修改版**：[`hichuv/HGhub`](https://github.com/hichuv/HGhub) > > 该仓库与本项目无关，是在旧版本源码基础上擅自加入**卡密验证、VIP 付费解锁**等变现功能的修改版， > 代码改动不透明、安全性无法验证。**请勿下载、勿注册、勿付费**；如已安装，建议立即卸载，改用官方 Release 包安装。 > > 本项目**从未、也不会**加入任何卡密 / VIP / 付费解锁 / 广告功能。如果你遇到的「HGhub」要求输入卡密或付费开通，那一定不是官方版本。 ## 技术栈 | 层 | 选型 | | --- | --- | | 壳 | Tauri 2（Rust 1.90+） | | 前端 | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7 + Tailwind CSS 4 | | 播放 | hls.js（HLS / AES-128） | | 网络 | reqwest + rustls | ## 目录 ``` . ├─ src/ 前端 │ ├─ api.ts 接口封装 + 本地媒体协议 URL │ ├─ store.tsx 全局状态（导航栈 / 用户 / 本地收藏 / 主题） │ ├─ html.ts 吃瓜正文清洗与图片代理 │ ├─ components/ Feed（播放页）/ VideoSurface / PlayerControls / Panels / UI │ └─ pages/ Home / Search / Category / Profile / Posts ├─ src-tauri/ Rust 后端 │ └─ src/ │ ├─ net.rs 请求层（边缘信封 + 重试） │ ├─ api.rs 业务命令 │ ├─ media.rs 封面解密 + HLS 代理 + 缓存 │ └─ session.rs token 持久化 └─ docs/API.md 接口文档 ``` ## 开发 / 构建 ```bash pnpm install # 首次安装 pnpm app:dev # 桌面端热重载 pnpm app:build # 打包：Windows → NSIS 安装程序；macOS → .app + .dmg ``` macOS 先装 Xcode Command Line Tools（`xcode-select --install`），打包目标写在 `src-tauri/tauri.macos.conf.json`（`app` + `dmg`，窗口用系统标题栏 Overlay）。 Android（需 Android SDK + NDK，并配置 `ANDROID_HOME` / `NDK_HOME`）： ```bash pnpm android:init # 首次生成 android 工程 pnpm android:dev # 真机 / 模拟器调试 pnpm android:build # 产出 APK ``` iOS（需 Xcode、xcodegen、CocoaPods 与 Apple 开发者账号；自行签名安装到自己的设备）： ```bash export APPLE_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<你的 Team ID> pnpm tauri ios init --ci # 首次生成 Xcode 工程（src-tauri/gen/apple） pnpm tauri ios build --export-method debugging # 产出 src-tauri/gen/apple/build/arm64/HGhub.ipa xcrun devicectl device install app --device <解压后的 Payload/HGhub.app> ``` 最低系统版本写在 `src-tauri/tauri.ios.conf.json`（iOS 15）。iOS 复用安卓的触屏界面；自定义协议与 macOS 相同，为 `hg://localhost`。 ### 环境注意 - 工程若放在 **exFAT** 盘（不支持符号链接），需保留 `.npmrc` 中的 `node-linker=hoisted`。 - pnpm 10 靠 `package.json` 的 `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` 放行 `esbuild`，否则 `vite build` 缺少二进制； pnpm 11 起该字段失效，白名单改在 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 的 `allowBuilds`（两处都保留）。 ## 实现要点 「设置 → 播放 → 启动时静音」默认开启，每次启动应用均静音，播放时可手动开启声音。关闭此选项后，下次启动恢复上次的静音状态；音量仍会记忆。 安全加固后的正文处理、FakeIP/内网限制、账号线路隔离及本地回归方法，见 [客户端内容与网络安全](docs/security.md)。镜像线路仅支持游客浏览，跨站点切换和首次升级后需要重新登录。 Mihomo 与 sing-box 分流规则、已知域名统计及导入方法，见 [网络分流规则](rules/README.md)。 1. **统一边缘信封**：站点把 `/api/**` 收敛为 `POST /api/edge/request`（`method/path/body(base64)/content_type` + `Authorization: Bearer`），本项目只对接这一个入口，无需处理 Cookie。 2. **封面解密**：封面为 AES-128-CBC 密文，Rust 侧解密后经自定义协议输出，前端 `` 直接使用。 3. **HLS 代理**：m3u8 与分片经自定义协议转发并改写 `#EXT-X-KEY` / 分片地址，绕开 WebView 的 CORS 与防盗链。 4. **自定义协议**：Windows / Android 为 `http://hg.localhost/*`，macOS 为 `hg://localhost/*`（Tauri 的平台差异）。 Rust 侧 `lib.rs` 与前端 `api.ts` 各自按平台生成一次基址，两处必须一致，否则封面与视频全部加载失败。 5. **不做签名逆向**：只复用浏览器同源行为，接口字段均有文档与实测样本。 ## 免责声明 - 本项目与内容提供方无任何关联，作者不参与内容的制作、上传与分发。 - 本项目仅在上述官方渠道发布；任何第三方修改版（尤其是加卡密、VIP 变现的版本）均与作者无关，请自行甄别。 - 使用者应自行遵守所在地法律法规；因使用本项目产生的任何后果由使用者自行承担。 - 若相关权利方认为本项目存在侵权，请通过 Issue 联系，我们会及时处理。 ## License [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](LICENSE) —— **仅限非商业用途**。 - **允许**：个人学习、研究、自用、爱好项目，以及在非营利组织内部使用；可以自由修改、二次开发。 - **禁止**：任何商业用途。包括但不限于打包出售、接入付费/会员/广告变现、作为收费服务或商业产品的一部分分发。 - **保留声明**：分发本项目或其修改版时，必须附带本许可证全文（或上面的链接）以及 `Required Notice` 声明行。 - 商业授权请通过 Issue 联系作者单独洽谈。 > 历史说明：v1.0.1 及更早版本以 MIT 发布，已发出的副本继续按 MIT 授权；自 **v1.1.0** 起的新版本一律适用 PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0。 ## 常见问题 **1. `pnpm install` 报 `ERR_PNPM_EISDIR ... symlink`** 工程放在 exFAT / FAT32 盘时无法创建符号链接，保留 `.npmrc` 里的 `node-linker=hoisted` 即可。 **2. `tauri android build` 报 `Failed to create a symbolic link ... jniLibs`** 同样是 exFAT 不支持符号链接。可手动把 Rust 产物拷进 jniLibs，再直接跑 Gradle： ```bash cp src-tauri/target/aarch64-linux-android/debug/libhuangguo_client_lib.so \ src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/ cd src-tauri/gen/android ./gradlew assembleDebug # Windows: gradlew.bat assembleDebug ``` 产物在 `src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/outputs/apk/`。 **3. Android 构建提示找不到 SDK / NDK** 需要设置 `ANDROID_HOME`（Android SDK 根目录）、`NDK_HOME`（`$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<版本>`）与 `JAVA_HOME`（JDK 17）。 **4. macOS 打开时提示「已损坏」或「无法验证开发者」** Release 里的 dmg 没有用 Apple 开发者证书签名和公证，从网上下载后会被 Gatekeeper 拦下。 把 HGhub 拖进「应用程序」后，在终端执行一次： ```bash xattr -cr /Applications/HGhub.app ``` ## LinuxDO https://linux.do/

items.title: NotRexed/Hookshot
items.description: A Native Recompilation Of The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Nintendo Switch 2 Remake
items.readme:
Hookshot

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2) running natively on Windows & Linux, with no emulator.

Status | Install and play | In-game menu | Problems | Build from source | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License

Hookshot is a static recompilation. The game's code is translated to C and compiled into a Windows or Linux program, the console's system software is reimplemented, and the Switch 2 graphics are rebuilt on Vulkan. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**.
> [!WARNING] > Some users report the file in releases to be a Trojan - it is not. Feel free to run it through any antivirus software Discord: https://discord.gg/DVQQJphbBf
> [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy. Everything the build creates (`hookshot.exe`, the generated code, the shader caches and your > saves) comes from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. ## Project status Experimental. Most testing so far has been around the start of the game. Players have reported on many PCs since: the table says what works and what does not yet. | What | Status | |---|---| | Kokiri Forest: reaching gameplay and walking around | ✅ Works | | Sound, controller, keyboard and saves | ✅ Works | | In-game menu, frame generation and upscaling | ✅ Works | | Flicker (the picture flashing too bright while moving) | ✅ Fixed in v2.0.2 ([#645](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/pull/645)) | | Ground fog vanishing when looking down | ✅ Fixed in v2.0.2 ([#638](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/pull/638)) | | Models with missing pieces (doors, fences, parts of trees) | ✅ Fixed where tested, more play needed | | Stutter when entering new areas | ⚠️ Still happens the first time you visit a place. The next visits are smooth | | Performance | ⚠️ Depends on the PC: some reach a steady 60 fps, others stay below it, more so in Hyrule Field | | Hyrule Field, Castle Town, Kakariko and the dungeons | ⚠️ Players got there, with open bugs: striped shadows in Hyrule Field ([#468](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/468)), some crashes ([#317](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/317), [#648](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/648)) | | Ultrawide | ⚠️ The 3D keeps its shape, but the HUD is stretched and the picture is softer | | NVIDIA cards | ✅ Works. The most tested | | AMD cards | ⚠️ Some tested: reports from the RX 6600, RX 7800 XT and RX 7900 XTX. Known issue: the game loses the GPU in the Deku Tree on the RX 6600 ([#708](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/708), [#614](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/614)) | | Intel cards | ❓ Few reports, many of them black screens or crashes ([#17](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/17)) | | Cards without mesh shaders (such as AMD RX 5000 and older) | ❌ Not supported: parts of the picture are missing. A fallback was tried and taken out again for now ([#640](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/640)) | | Linux | ✅ Works with the AppImage. Tested on several distributions (CachyOS, Fedora, Bazzite, SteamOS) and cards, with open problems on some AMD cards ([#604](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/604), [#528](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/528)) | ## Install and play The game does not come ready-made: Hookshot Builder builds it on your PC from your copy. You do this once. After that you start the game from its launcher, which also updates it. ### What you need - **Your copy of the game at the supported version:** program `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072, build `e0f3ccfa`. Other versions do not work. A `.nup` file, or the `romfs` and `exefs` folders. - 64-bit Windows 10 or 11, or 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora, Arch, SteamOS ...) and a CPU with AVX2. - A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and mesh shaders, with an up-to-date driver: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 series or newer, AMD Radeon RX 6000 series or newer, or Intel Arc. On Linux, Mesa or NVIDIA's driver. Cards without mesh shaders are not supported. - 8 GB of video memory (VRAM) or more is recommended. Cards with less can use the in-game menu's lower Quality presets. - 16 GB of RAM or more. A run uses about 10 GB. - About 60 GB free while building. - An internet connection for the download. Nothing else to install: the builder brings its own compiler and tools. ### On Windows 1. Open the [latest release](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/releases/latest) and download `HookshotBuilder.exe`. 2. Run it. It downloads the rest of Hookshot Builder (about 500 MB), checks it, and opens it. 3. Pick your game. The builder looks for `.nup` files in your Downloads, Desktop and Documents folders and lists them under **Found on this PC**. Not listed? Press **Browse…**, drop the file on the window, or choose **romfs and exefs folders**. The builder checks that it is the right version. 4. Under **Install the game to**, keep the folder (`Games\Hookshot` in your user folder) or press **Change**. Choose the **Game language**. 5. Press **Build the game**. It takes about 10 to 45 minutes, depending on your CPU and memory. You can use your PC in the meantime. 6. When it says **Your game is ready**, press **Play**. The **Desktop shortcut** and **Start menu entry** boxes are ticked: untick them if you don't want them. Next time, start the game from the Hookshot shortcut, or `hookshot.exe` in the game folder. That is the launcher: it has **Play**, and **Update** when a newer release is out. The first start prepares the game's shaders, which takes a while. Later starts are faster. ### On Linux 1. Open the [latest release](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/releases/latest) and download `Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage`. It is Hookshot Builder with everything it needs inside. 2. Allow it to run as a program. In most file managers: right-click it, open **Properties**, and turn on "Allow executing file as program" (the words differ between desktops). Or in a terminal: `chmod +x Hookshot-*-x86_64.AppImage`. 3. Double-click it. The Hookshot Builder window opens. 4. Under **Game files**, choose **.nup file** or **romfs and exefs**, then press **Browse** to pick them. The builder checks the version. 5. Under **Save the game to**, keep `~/Games/Hookshot` or choose another folder. Choose a **Language**. 6. Press **Build**. It takes about 10 to 45 minutes, depending on your CPU and memory. 7. When it says "Your game is ready", press **Play**. The game is also added to your applications menu as "Hookshot". That entry, and `hookshot` in the game folder, open the launcher: **Play**, and **Update** when a newer release is out. Keep the AppImage where it is: the launcher uses it to update. ### Updating When a new release is out, the launcher says "Update available". Press **Update**: in `hookshot.exe` on Windows, or in `hookshot` (or the AppImage) on Linux. It downloads only the parts that changed and builds the game again in the same folder, compiling only what changed. Your saves and settings are kept. What changed is on the [Releases page](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/releases).
What an update keeps and replaces, and updating from the command line To be safe, copy your saves somewhere first: the `user` folder in the game folder on Windows, or `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux. | Kept | Replaced | |---|---| | Your saves (`user`, or `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux) | The game in `bin` and its files | | `hookshot_options.ini`, the in-game menu's choices and your controls | `image.bin` and the shader list | | `hookshot_env.txt` | `language.txt`, written again with the game's language | | `mods` | | The game files the first build read are kept in the game folder, so an update does not need your `.nup` again. From a clone: `git pull`, then `python -I nx2/make_game.py --update `. The Linux AppImage does the same with `--update `.
### Where the files go - The build reads your game and never changes it. It writes to the folder you choose and to the builder's own folder: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder` on Windows, `~/.cache/hookshot-builder` on Linux. - The romfs is hard-linked instead of copied where the disk allows it. - The builder keeps its build files (about 4 GB) so that updates are quick. None of them are needed to play: on Windows, **Free up space** on the "Your game is ready" page deletes them, and the build files folder can be moved before a build (**Change**, **Default**). - Saves: the `user` folder in the game folder on Windows, `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux (a `user` folder from an earlier Linux build is moved there once). `--user ` puts them somewhere else ([command line arguments](#running-the-game-from-the-command-line)). - To uninstall, delete the game folder, the builder's folder and the shortcuts. ### If something goes wrong | Problem | What to do | |---|---| | Where is the log? | `hookshot_log.txt` in the game folder holds the last run. The four runs before are `hookshot_log.1.txt` (the last) to `.4.txt`. Started from a terminal, the game prints there instead | | "Hookshot supports build e0f3ccfa" or "This version isn't supported" | Check that you chose the right game with its update installed | | The game opens and closes, or the log says "device lost" | Update your graphics driver. On AMD cards there are known crashes ([#708](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/708), [#614](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/614)) | | Parts of the picture are missing, or a message says your card has no mesh shader support | The card or its driver has no mesh shaders. Update the driver; older cards are not supported ([#640](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/640)) | | Linux: the game does not start or the picture is broken | The game needs a Vulkan 1.3 driver with mesh shaders. Check with `vulkaninfo \| grep mesh`: it should list `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`. Update Mesa or the NVIDIA driver | | "Your antivirus removed part of the build tools" | A false alarm on unsigned programs. Restore the files from Windows Security's Protection history, or add `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder` to its exclusions, then press **Repair** | | Stutter the first time you see something | Normal for now: shaders are being prepared. It gets better when you pass through the same place again | | The game is in the wrong language | Change the code in `language.txt` in the game folder. The file lists them all | If the problem continues, [report it](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/new/choose) with the version, where you were in the game, your graphics card, `hookshot_log.txt` and a screenshot or video. Never send game files. ## In-game menu Press Insert (or F1) in game, or on a controller the Home button (or Select and Start together). The same keys close it, and so does Esc. The menu has three tabs, Graphics, Gameplay and Controls: Q and E (or Tab and Shift+Tab) switch between them, LB and RB on a controller. Up and Down choose a row, Left and Right change it (Enter changes it too). On a controller the D-pad chooses and changes, the bottom face button changes too, and the right one closes the menu. Your choices are saved in `hookshot_options.ini` in the game folder. | Tab | Option | Choices | Default | |---|---|---|---| | Graphics | Quality preset | Custom, Minimum (4GB), Low (6GB), Balanced (8GB), High (12GB), Ultra (16GB+) | Custom | | | Fullscreen | Off, On (the same as F11) | Off | | | GPU device | Auto, or each graphics card by name (after a restart) | Auto | | | Frame generation | Off, 2x to 8x | Off | | | Frame pacing | Off, On | Off | | | Resolution | Auto (the game's own dynamic resolution), 100%, 75%, 67%, 50% (each with its size) | Auto | | | Output resolution | 2048x1152, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 (after a restart) | 2048x1152 | | | Upscaling | Off, Catmull-Rom, Lanczos | Off | | | Sharpness | 0 to 100%, in steps of 10 | 0% | | | Handheld profile | Off, On (after a restart) | Off | | | Ultrawide | 16:9, Monitor's shape (after a restart) | 16:9 | | | Robust buffers | Auto, Off, On (after a restart) | Auto | | Gameplay | FPS counter | Off, On | Off | | | Game speed | Per frame, Real time | Real time | | | Text speed | Normal, 2x, 4x, Instant | Normal | | Controls | Controller in background | Off, On | Off | | | Mouse camera | As the stick, Native | As the stick | | | Mouse sensitivity | 0.10 to 5.00 | 1.00 | | | Invert mouse vertical | Off, On | Off | | | Invert camera X | Off, On | Off | | | Invert camera Y | Off, On | Off | | | Layout preset | Nintendo (Def), Xbox / PC, Swap Face, Custom | Nintendo (Def) | | | Controls | Opens the Controls page | | - **Quality preset** sets Resolution, Upscaling, Sharpness, Frame generation, Frame pacing, Game speed, Handheld profile and the video memory limits for a card with that much memory. Changing most other rows yourself sets it back to Custom. - **GPU device** matters on a PC with more than one graphics card (a laptop's integrated and dedicated GPUs, or a second card for Lossless Scaling). Auto prefers a dedicated one, and only cards with Vulkan 1.3 are listed. `hookshot_log.txt` lists every card as `vk: device `; `RX_VK_DEVICE=` chooses one for a single run and wins over the menu. - **Frame generation** makes extra frames between the game's own. It adds a little input delay, and fast motion can show artifacts. **Frame pacing** shows frames at an even interval: less stutter, up to one frame of delay. - **Output resolution** is the size of the game's whole frame, HUD included, before it is scaled to your window. Resolution is a share of it, and its row shows the size for the output you chose. Docked only. At 3840x2160 the game's render targets get a bigger GPU pool, so a full-size 3D fits. `HOS_OUTPUT_RES=0/1/2` sets it for one run. - **Upscaling** and **Sharpness** also work when Frame generation is Off. - **Handheld profile** runs the game as if the console were undocked: lower resolution, lighter on the GPU. - **Robust buffers:** a read past a buffer's end is dropped instead of stopping the GPU. Auto is on, on every card; Off can be faster on some NVIDIA cards. - **Game speed:** with Per frame, the game runs slower whenever it is below 60 fps. Real time keeps it at normal speed down to 15 fps. - **FPS counter** shows in the top right corner. With frame generation on, it also shows the game's own rate. - **Controller in background:** On keeps the controller working while another window has the focus. The keyboard and mouse still need the game's window. - **Mouse camera:** Native turns the camera with the mouse one to one, as in a PC game. As the stick uses the mouse in place of the right stick. The - and = keys change the sensitivity in game too. - **Layout preset:** Nintendo has A on the right face button, Xbox / PC and Swap Face put A on the bottom one. Changing a button yourself sets it to Custom. ### Controls Use a controller, or the keyboard and mouse. On the keyboard, W A S D move and the arrow keys (or I J K L) turn the camera. To change which gamepad button or key presses a Switch button, or which keys move and turn the camera, open the Controls tab's Controls page. Choose a row and a column (Gamepad or Keyboard), press Enter (or the bottom face button), then the new button or key. Esc cancels, Delete clears it, and Reset to defaults puts them all back. A gamepad button taken from another Switch button swaps with it. The page saves them in `hookshot_options.ini`.
Writing the controls in hookshot_options.ini yourself ```ini pad_a=0 key_a=69,13 ``` `pad_
## Mods Put mods in a `mods` folder in the game folder, beside `hookshot.exe` (or point `HOS_MODS` at another folder), in the layout emulators use: `mods//romfs/...` holds files that replace or add to the game's own. Deeper layouts such as `mods/contents//<name>/romfs` work too. A folder whose name starts with `-` or `_` is off. When two mods have the same file, the one whose folder name sorts last wins, so name them `01-...`, `02-...` to set the order. Only RomFS mods are loaded. `exefs` patches (`.pchtxt`, `.ips`) are left out: Hookshot compiles the game's code ahead of time, so patching its instructions would need a rebuild. The log (`hookshot_log.txt`) names each mod and the files read from it. ## Build from source For developers, and for players who prefer the command line. The builder windows run the same script, `nx2/make_game.py`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has more. <details> <summary>Windows, from the command line</summary> ```powershell python -I nx2/make_game.py --nup "C:\path\your-game.nup" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US python -I nx2/make_game.py --romfs "C:\path\romfs" --exefs "C:\path\exefs" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US ``` Add `--check` with your `.nup` or `--exefs` to only check the game's version. It builds nothing. Add `--log "C:\path\build.log"` to also save the build's output to a file (UTF-8, replaced if it exists); it works with `--check` and `--update` too, and on Linux. `HOOKSHOT_JOBS=<n>` (or `--jobs <n>`) limits how many files compile at once. You need: - Python 3 from python.org (the Microsoft Store's Python installs packages where `python -I` does not look), with `pip install lz4 numpy capstone "unicorn>=2.1,<2.2" zstandard`. - [llvm-mingw](https://github.com/mstorsjo/llvm-mingw) (the `ucrt-x86_64` build), unpacked as `llvm-mingw` in the clone or with `HOOKSHOT_MINGW` set to its folder. Without it the build uses the clang from [emsdk](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk) at `C:\emsdk` with Visual Studio's C++ tools and the Windows SDK (`HOOKSHOT_MSVC=1` forces that route). - What the builder's `tools` folder carries and a clone does not. Run `HookshotBuilder.exe` once: the folder is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder\versions\<version>\HookshotBuilder\tools`. The builder sets the variables itself; from the command line, set them before you run `make_game.py`: - `tools\cpm`: the Vulkan headers and FFmpeg. Set `RX_CPM` to this folder. Without it the build leaves out `hookshot_vk.dll`, the Vulkan renderer, and says nothing. - `tools\wgpu-native`: set `WGPU_NATIVE` to this folder. - `tools\third_party`: the prebuilt files a clone lacks (`a64emit`, `lld-link`, `zbic` and SDL2). Copy its `.dll`, `.exe`, `.lib` and `.sha1` files to the same places under `third_party\`. - `tools\work`: copy it to `work\`. It holds the hot-function list, the link order, the profile and the icon; without them the game builds but runs slower. - Visual Studio 2022 with .NET 8, only if you want to change the builder itself. </details> <details> <summary>Linux, the AppImage from the command line</summary> ```sh ./Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage --cli --nup ~/your-game.nup --out ~/Games/Hookshot # make_game.py's options ./Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage --play # the game the builder built last, without the window ./Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage --play ~/Games/Hookshot # the game in that folder ./Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage --update ~/Games/Hookshot # the new release, and that folder built again ``` `HOOKSHOT_JOBS=<n>` (or `--jobs <n>` with `--cli`) limits how many files compile at once. In a game folder, `hookshot` is the launcher and the game itself is `bin/hookshot`. The builder's settings are in `~/.config/hookshot/builder.ini`. </details> <details> <summary>Linux, without the AppImage</summary> You need `clang` and `lld` (LLVM 23 or newer reads the play profile; an older one builds without it), Python 3 with `lz4`, `numpy`, `capstone`, `unicorn` and `zstandard`, FFmpeg's development files (with dav1d, for the movies) and SDL3 (SDL2 works too). Then run `python -I nx2/make_game.py ...` as on Windows, with `RX_CPM` pointing at a folder with Vulkan-Headers, SPIRV-Headers and VulkanMemoryAllocator in CPM's layout. `scripts/linux/deps.sh` fetches and builds all of these into `build-linux/deps`, and `scripts/linux/appimage.sh` makes the AppImage from them. A folder built from a source checkout has no launcher: `hookshot` there is the game. </details> <details> <summary>The Windows game, built on Linux</summary> Unpack llvm-mingw's Linux build (`ucrt-ubuntu-22.04-x86_64`), then run `make_game.py` with `RX_TARGET=windows` and `HOOKSHOT_MINGW` set to its folder. The objects go to `~/.cache/hookshot-builder-windows`, apart from the Linux game's. The game folder runs under Proton or on Windows. </details> ### Running the game from the command line The built game is `bin\hookshot.exe` on Windows and `bin/hookshot` in a packaged Linux game folder. A build from a source checkout has `hookshot.exe` or `hookshot` in its build folder, with no launcher beside it. The `hookshot.exe` or `hookshot` launcher in the game folder does not pass these arguments to the game, so start the game directly to use them. | Argument | What it does | |---|---| | `image.bin` | The game image to run. Without it the game uses the `image.bin`, `romfs` and `user` in its folder | | `--romfs <folder>` | The extracted RomFS folder | | `--user <folder>` | Where the game keeps per-user data: saves, caches, temp files and `mouse_sens.txt`. Default: `user` in the game folder on Windows, `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux; with an explicit image path, `user` in the current folder | | `--trace` | Log every Horizon OS call (the same as `HOS_TRACE=1`) | | `--prepare-shaders` | Prepare the shaders and exit without starting the game (the build's last step) | For example, keep saves somewhere else: ```powershell cd "C:\Games\Hookshot" .\bin\hookshot.exe --user "D:\Hookshot data" ``` ```sh cd ~/Games/Hookshot ./bin/hookshot --user "$HOME/hookshot-data" ``` `hookshot_env.txt` and the other test switches are documented below. <details> <summary>Switches for testing (hookshot_env.txt)</summary> Switches to test (`RX_VK_NOOPT=1` and the others) go in `hookshot_env.txt` in the game folder, one `NAME=VALUE` a line, on Windows and Linux. The running game reads it, not the builder. A test run can name another file with `HOS_ENV_FILE=<path>`; the game then reads that one instead and leaves `hookshot_env.txt` alone. For a first run on a 4 GB card such as a GTX 1650, `RX_VK_LOW_SPEC=1` starts with the Minimum (4GB) preset, with frame generation and upscaling off. It applies only when there is no `hookshot_options.ini` yet; after that, change the settings in the in-game menu. `RX_VK_MOVIE_UPSCALE=linear` replaces the movies' neural upscale with the plain linear one. The default, `auto`, keeps the networks and falls back only when a movie frame takes the GPU more than 40 ms. It does not change the gameplay upscaler, and movies can look softer. `RX_VK_NETWORK_KEEP=all` takes precedence and keeps the movie networks. </details> ## How it works 1. `nx2/lift.py` translates the game's ARM64 code to C. 2. `nx2/build.py` compiles that C together with `host/`, which plays the part of the console's system. 3. `host/nvn_native.c` records the game's NVN2 graphics calls, and `gpu/vk/` replays them on Vulkan. 4. Switch 2 Ampere shaders are lowered to Maxwell (`lower_to_maxwell.h`) and translated to SPIR-V by Eden's shader recompiler. More detail is in the [development guide](docs/development.md) and the [design notes](docs/design.md). ## Want to help? Testing on other graphics cards and reporting the result already helps a lot, and so does playing further into the game than anyone has yet. Bigger ways to help: - **Linux testing.** The Linux build (`host/posix`) has been tested on several distributions and cards: reports from others still help. - **Fixes in your own fork.** Fork the project, fix what you find and send the change back. Keep game files, keys and anything generated from your game out of it. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the setup, the test commands, the code conventions and what a good pull request looks like. ## Credits Hookshot exists thanks to the work of many people: - **NotRexed**: Hookshot, BlueShell (Mario Kart World), Skybound (Tears of the Kingdom) and the a64-kit tools. - **[Eden](https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden)** and **Eglantine**: the shader recompiler and Switch 2 shader work. - **suyu**: the graphics decoders and the AArch64 translator. - **[seedds/nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)**: reference for how task and mesh shaders work. - **[EvilBoyce / evilmfkr](https://github.com/evilmfkr/Hookshot)** (EvilOOT): the GPU culling that brings back Kokiri's foliage (trees, ferns, grass, falling leaves, fireflies), the ambient light probes, the pond's water, the game's own fog, the freeze after Load (Horizon's mutex handoff) and the exposure flicker fix. - **[zortos293/Lichii](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii)**: reference for Ampere shader lowering, and its compare-exchange retry fix. - **[mstorsjo/llvm-mingw](https://github.com/mstorsjo/llvm-mingw)**: the bundled Windows compiler (no Visual Studio needed). - **[kinnay/zbic](https://github.com/kinnay/zbic)**, **Opus** and **SDL**: decompression, audio and controllers. - **[sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp](https://github.com/sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp)**: this README's layout, and its notes confirmed the mesh stage's control section. - **[MythosOfs/Orchid](https://github.com/MythosOfs/Orchid)**: the fog and exposure workaround for Ocarina of Time. - **Mesa (NAK)**: the reference for Ampere's instruction encoding. - Everyone who sent fixes: SkippySteve (Linux and the AppImage, and many more), monsterlag, klimovich008, hckrman101 (the exposure flicker and fog fixes, build speed, CI), shayderrr, gab9281, Wpaif, nicholasgower, ZurielAtr, Joey-Magnus, Zorkats, d3zessete, chrispository, vzeol, leonidasmark, Segmentree, ShyVortex, hiKareeem and i900gaming, among others. ## License Hookshot is free software under the [GNU General Public License, version 3 or later](LICENSE) (GPL-3.0-or-later). It includes code from Eden, suyu and Orchid, which are under the GPL too. Third-party parts under other licenses that work with the GPL (Sirit, the Vulkan Memory Allocator, SDL, Opus, stb, zbic and the a64-kit tools) keep their own notices in their folders. Hookshot is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. The Legend of Zelda and Ocarina of Time are trademarks of Nintendo.

items.title: govijr/terminal-mac
items.description: Entire MacOS running in your terminal.
items.readme: # terminal-mac [![](https://img.shields.io/static/v1?label=Sponsor&message=%E2%9D%A4&logo=GitHub&color=%23fe8e86)](https://github.com/sponsors/govijr) A separate macOS desktop for computer-use agents, viewed and controlled from a terminal. `terminal-mac` is an early release candidate for Apple silicon. Apple Virtualization runs a real macOS guest. A bundled helper **inside that guest** captures its screen and posts input events. A terminal viewer streams that screen using Kitty or iTerm2 graphics. Agent commands use the same helper without moving the physical Mac's pointer or changing its clipboard. The guest is a separate Mac: it has its own apps, files, accounts and permissions. It does not inherit your running host apps or signed-in sessions. The VM still consumes host CPU, memory and storage. ## Requirements - Apple silicon Mac, macOS 14 or later. - No development tools are needed for a prebuilt release. Maintainers need Xcode 16 or later / Swift 6 to build. - Internet on first run to download macOS directly from Apple, or an existing compatible `.ipsw`. - Space for the cached restore image and a growing VM disk (64 GiB logical size by default). - Ghostty, Kitty or iTerm2 for the inline viewer. Other terminals can use the native VM window and agent CLI. tmux passthrough and automatic terminal splits are not implemented. ## Install and run ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/govijr/terminal-mac/releases/latest/download/get.sh | bash ``` The installer downloads the latest release and verifies its SHA-256 before installing. You can also extract a release ZIP and run `bash install.sh` from it. The installer places one launcher in `~/.local/bin` and the bundled runtime under `~/.local/lib/terminal-mac`. Add `~/.local/bin` to your PATH to use simply `terminal-mac`. It needs no administrator rights and does not edit your shell configuration. `bash install.sh --prefix /absolute/path` selects another location. Running `terminal-mac` in an interactive terminal starts the guided flow. `terminal-mac up` does the same explicitly. It automatically downloads/caches a compatible Apple restore image, installs a virtual Mac, boots it and checks the guest helper. Later runs reuse the existing VM and reconnect. Unsupported terminals get the native desktop window. **Current status:** early release candidate. Releases are self-signed (no Apple notarization), which the curl installer doesn't need. Live guest acceptance on a clean Mac is still pending. ## Use with agents terminal-mac gives agents computer use in a separate virtual Mac, through MCP tools (`screenshot`, `click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`, `status`) and a skill that teaches the observe → act → verify loop. **Claude Code**, with the MCP server and skill in one plugin: ```text /plugin install terminal-mac --marketplace govijr/terminal-mac ``` Or add them separately: ```sh claude mcp add terminal-mac -- terminal-mac mcp terminal-mac skills install # → ~/.claude/skills/terminal-mac/SKILL.md ``` **Other MCP clients** (Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Windsurf…): paste the output of `terminal-mac mcp --config` into the client's MCP settings. Use `terminal-mac mcp NAME` for a VM other than `default`. **Any agent with a skills folder:** `terminal-mac skills install --dir PATH`, or `npx skills add govijr/terminal-mac --skill terminal-mac`. In an `AGENTS.md`, a line like "Before using the virtual Mac, run `terminal-mac skills get`" gives the agent instructions that match the installed version. The tools only drive the guest helper. They never touch your own desktop. When the guest is at its login screen, they say so, so the agent can ask you to sign in. ## One-time guest setup The first run opens the virtual Mac's window. Complete macOS setup and create its user account. Inside the guest, open Finder → `/Volumes/My Shared Files/tools` → `TerminalMacGuest.app` once. The helper installs itself in the guest's `~/Applications`, launches that installed copy and registers for future guest logins, subject to macOS approval. Use its two buttons to grant **Screen Recording** and **Accessibility** inside the guest. Reopen it if macOS asks. If needed, its **Guest Login Items** button opens the startup setting. The host needs neither privacy permission. Once both guest permissions are ready, the CLI automatically continues to the terminal desktop. This is guided setup, not an unattended guest installation. Apple documents automatic account provisioning for macOS 27 guests; this build targets the APIs available in the installed macOS 26 SDK and does not implement that newer flow. See [Apple's provisioning documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/virtualization/vzmacguestprovisioningoptions). ```sh terminal-mac up work # another virtual Mac terminal-mac up --ipsw /path/mac.ipsw # use a local image terminal-mac up --no-view # wait for agent readiness, then return JSON terminal-mac up --detach # install/boot, return without waiting for guest setup terminal-mac up --plan # show steps without network access or disk changes ``` The first download may take time; packaging cannot eliminate downloading and installing macOS. The image cache is reused, and URLSession resume data is retained after recoverable network failures. A hard process kill may require the current download to restart. An incomplete installation with recorded hardware can be retried by `up` using a compatible restore image; an already installed VM is never reinstalled by `up`. ## Build from source ```sh bash scripts/build.sh ./dist/terminal-mac doctor ``` The build creates `dist/TerminalMac.app`, including `TerminalMacGuest.app`, and the `dist/terminal-mac` launcher. Virtualization needs the host executable's `com.apple.security.virtualization` entitlement; use the packaged launcher instead of the unsigned Swift build product. It is signed with the self-signed "Govijr Code Signing" identity when your keychain has it (`bash scripts/create-signing-identity.sh` makes one), and ad-hoc otherwise. A stable identity keeps the guest helper's permissions across rebuilds; ad-hoc builds need them granted again. [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) covers signing and publishing. ## Create your first Mac ```sh # Show the URL and version without downloading anything: ./dist/terminal-mac image # Explicitly download Apple's latest supported restore image (several GB): ./dist/terminal-mac image --output /tmp/RestoreImage.ipsw # Install macOS. The disk is sparse, and the IPSW is not copied into the VM bundle. ./dist/terminal-mac create default --ipsw /tmp/RestoreImage.ipsw ./dist/terminal-mac start default --window ``` Complete macOS Setup Assistant in the VM window and create a guest account. Inside the guest: 1. Open Finder → `/Volumes/My Shared Files/tools`. 2. Open `TerminalMacGuest.app`. It installs itself to the guest's `~/Applications` and opens the installed copy. 3. Use the helper's buttons to grant **Screen Recording** and **Accessibility** in the guest's System Settings. Reopen the helper if macOS asks. The host does not need either permission. 4. Keep the guest logged in and the helper running. It registers itself for guest login; approve that setting if macOS requests it. On the host: ```sh ./dist/terminal-mac action default status ./dist/terminal-mac hide default ./dist/terminal-mac view default ``` The viewer supports typing, left/right clicks, double and triple clicks, dragging, scrolling, arrows and common control keys. **Ctrl+G** opens a palette of Mac shortcuts (Spotlight, Mission Control, copy/paste, close/quit and more), because terminals keep ⌘ for themselves. **Ctrl+]** exits the viewer while the VM keeps running. Closing the native VM window hides it and also leaves the VM running. The guest helper keeps a ScreenCaptureKit stream open while a viewer is watching. It sends a frame only when the screen changes (up to 30 fps), already sized to the pixels the terminal draws, as lossless lz4-compressed pixels. Kitty and Ghostty receive those frames through shared memory rather than the pty. An idle desktop costs nothing, and the stream stops 15 seconds after the viewer leaves. From build 4 on, the guest helper updates itself: within 30 seconds of a newer build appearing in the shared tools folder, it installs that build and relaunches. Helpers from build 3 and earlier still work but poll full screenshots, and the header shows "snapshots". Update those once by opening `/Volumes/My Shared Files/tools/TerminalMacGuest.app` in the guest. Releases are signed with one unchanging self-signed certificate, so the guest keeps its Screen Recording and Accessibility approvals across updates. Guest helper updates must satisfy the running helper's designated code requirement. Stable certificate-signed builds retain their update identity. An ad-hoc rebuild generally has a different code identity and is refused by automatic updates; install it manually inside the guest and grant its permissions again. Agents can drive the guest through an MCP server: `claude mcp add terminal-mac -- "$PWD/dist/terminal-mac" mcp default`. See [docs/AGENT.md](docs/AGENT.md). New VMs use a 2x HiDPI display (for example 2560×1600 pixels at 220 ppi for the default 1280×800 points), so text stays sharp on Retina terminals. Switch a stopped VM with `terminal-mac display default --hidpi` or `--standard`. The automounted volume is supplied by macOS virtio-fs. If it is absent, check the guest's macOS version and the VM log; this prototype has no fallback guest transport. ## Give an agent computer control ```sh ./dist/terminal-mac action default screenshot --output /tmp/guest.png ./dist/terminal-mac action default click 640 400 ./dist/terminal-mac action default type 'Hello from the agent' ./dist/terminal-mac action default key cmd+space ./dist/terminal-mac action default key return ./dist/terminal-mac action default scroll --dy -300 --x 640 --y 400 ``` Commands return JSON and a nonzero exit status on failure. Screenshots return a local host PNG path. Coordinates start at the top-left and match the screenshot's dimensions; screenshots use guest display points to keep input coordinates consistent on Retina displays. `snapshot` is currently a screenshot alias, not an accessibility-tree snapshot. The agent instructions are in [docs/AGENT.md](docs/AGENT.md). No global agent settings are modified. ## Lifecycle and resources ```sh ./dist/terminal-mac ls ./dist/terminal-mac status default ./dist/terminal-mac pause default ./dist/terminal-mac resume default ./dist/terminal-mac show default ./dist/terminal-mac stop default # request a normal guest shutdown ./dist/terminal-mac stop default --force # immediate power-off; unsaved guest work can be lost ``` Customize a new VM with `--cpus 4 --memory 4 --disk 64 --width 1280 --height 800` (width and height are in points; add `--standard` for a 1x display). CPU, memory and disk arguments are logical CPUs, GiB and GiB respectively. `--offline` omits the guest network device; the shared-folder control channel still works, though some macOS setup workflows may require networking. VM data lives in `~/Library/Application Support/terminal-mac/machines/NAME/`. `TERMINAL_MAC_HOME` overrides the data root. Each VM has an exclusive file lock, a sparse disk, hardware identity, auxiliary boot storage, `machine.json`, a private host-control mailbox, the guest exchange directory, and `runtime.log`. A VM boot runs as a separate background process. Lifecycle commands must use the same `TERMINAL_MAC_HOME` as the process that started it. An interrupted or failed installation leaves its directory and `installed: false` for diagnosis. It is never silently overwritten. To retry, ensure no installer/VM is running, move that incomplete directory aside, then create the VM again. There is deliberately no destructive VM-delete command yet. ## Isolation model - Host input and screen APIs are not used for agent actions. The helper refuses to run unless `hw.model` starts with `VirtualMac`. That check prevents accidental host execution; it is not hardware attestation or a defense against a compromised host. - The guest sees two explicit shares: `control` (read/write, containing request/reply JSON and screenshots) and `tools` (read-only helper app). Host home, project folders, clipboard, microphone, and camera are not attached. - There is no remote-control network listener. The flat mailbox pins its directory, rejects symlinks, hardlinks and nonregular files on reads, bounds message sizes, checks request IDs, and expires pending actions. The host never executes guest-provided content. - Default NAT networking permits guest internet access and may reach services on the host or local network. This is **not** a network-isolated or hardened hostile-code environment. `--offline` removes that network path. - A logged-out/locked guest, missing helper, denied guest permissions, or paused VM prevents normal computer use. TCC grants are interactive guest setup, not bypassed by the CLI. VM cloning, rollback checkpoints, accessibility snapshots, fully unattended guest setup, terminal splits and tmux transport remain future work. The native Virtualization framework does not itself render a Mac into a terminal or offer an agent input API; this project supplies the guest transport and terminal presentation layers. ## Development and validation ```sh CLANG_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/terminal-mac-modules \ SWIFTPM_MODULECACHE_OVERRIDE=/tmp/terminal-mac-modules \ swift test --disable-sandbox --scratch-path /tmp/terminal-mac-build \ --cache-path /tmp/terminal-mac-cache \ --config-path /tmp/terminal-mac-config --security-path /tmp/terminal-mac-security ``` Tests cover mailbox round trips, expiry and cleanup, file-boundary defenses, name/option validation, fragmented UTF-8 and terminal input sequences. These are automated protocol checks, not evidence that a guest was installed, booted, granted permissions, or controlled successfully. See [docs/VALIDATION.md](docs/VALIDATION.md) for recorded results and the live checklist. References: [terminal-browser](https://terminal-browser.com/), [Apple's macOS virtualization sample](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/virtualization/running-macos-in-a-virtual-machine-on-apple-silicon), [VZVirtualMachineView](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/virtualization/vzvirtualmachineview), [ScreenCaptureKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/screencapturekit). ## Sponsor terminal-mac is free and maintained in my own time. [Sponsoring](https://github.com/sponsors/govijr) keeps it that way.
