items.title: egoist/mygo-music
items.description: A native music player you extend with plugins
items.readme:
# MyGo Music

A native desktop music player written in Go with [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo), no WebView. It plays your local files out of the box, and everything else comes from plugins.

## Features

- Local files (MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, WAV, and ALAC, FLAC or AAC in .m4a and .aac) with tags, covers and `.lrc` lyrics
- Playlists, liked songs, search, albums and artists
- Now Playing with lyric stage styles, cover wall, queue, shuffle and repeat
- Notch player on macOS, tray, media keys
- Audio cache, fades on pause and seek, loudness normalization
- Session restore
- Podcast captions, written down on the device as episodes play
- English and Simplified Chinese
- Plugins can add accounts, catalogs, podcasts, stations, comments and pages of their own

## Build

```bash
go tool mygo dev     # run in development
go tool mygo build   # package into build/
go test ./internal/...
```

## Podcast captions

Episodes are written down on the device as they play, with [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) and Qwen3-ASR, which the app downloads when the listener asks for them. The libraries come from this repository's `sherpa-onnx-<version>` prerelease, which only changes with that version:

```bash
go run ./scripts/sherpa -sign "Developer ID Application: …"
gh release create sherpa-onnx-2.0.1 --prerelease --latest=false build/sherpa/*
```

## Plugins

A plugin is a folder in the app's `plugins` directory (Settings > Plugins > + > Show Plugins Folder) with a `plugin.json` and one JavaScript or TypeScript file. Install one with the + in Settings > Plugins from GitHub, by its repository or its address, or from its folder or a zip of it on this computer, or drop the folder in by hand. Remove one from its ⋯ menu there. There's nothing to build, and the same plugin runs on every platform. [`examples/demo-plugin`](examples/demo-plugin) does everything a plugin can with made-up data: copy it to start.

```json
{
  "id": "example",
  "name": "Example",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "minAppVersion": "0.1.8",
  "main": "index.js",
  "playback": "stream",
  "permissions": { "network": ["api.example.com"] },
  "settings": [{ "key": "apiKey", "label": "API Key", "help": "From your account page", "link": "https://example.com/keys" }],
  "navigation": [
    { "builtin": "home" },
    { "title": "Charts", "page": "charts", "icon": "chart" },
    { "title": "Stations", "builtin": "stations" }
  ]
}
```

```js
export async function search({ query, kind, offset }) {
  const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&type=${kind}&offset=${offset}`, {
    headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${host.setting("apiKey")}` },
  });
  return { tracks: (await res.json()).items.map(toTrack), more: false };
}

export function stream({ id, quality }) {
  return { url: `https://api.example.com/audio/${id}.mp3`, type: "mp3" };
}
```

Export a function for each thing the plugin does. Each takes one object of parameters and returns a value or a promise. What it doesn't export, the app leaves out of its pages.

| Export | Parameters | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `signIn`, `signOut`, `account` | | `{id, name, imageUrl, page}`; `account` returns `null` when signed out. `page` is a `browse` page of the listener's own, which the account menu opens as My Page |
| `setSetting` | `{key, value}` | |
| `home` | | `Browse` |
| `browse` | `{page}` | `Browse` |
| `search` | `{query, kind, offset}`, where `kind` is `tracks`, `albums`, `artists`, `playlists` or `shows` | `{tracks or albums or ..., more}` |
| `suggest` | `{query}` | `[string]` |
| `recent` | | `[Track]` |
| `played` | `{id}` | |
| `liked` | `{offset}` | `{tracks, more}` |
| `isLiked` | `{ids}` | `{id: bool}` |
| `like`, `likeEpisode` | `{id, on}` | `like` likes a song, and `likeEpisode` an episode: without it, episodes show no heart |
| `album` | `{id}` | `{album, tracks}` |
| `artist` | `{id}` | `{artist, tracks, albums}` |
| `saveAlbum`, `followArtist`, `savePlaylist`, `subscribeShow` | `{id, on}` | |
| `savedAlbums` | `{offset}` | `{albums, more}` |
| `playlists` | | `[Playlist]` |
| `playlist` | `{id}` | `Playlist` with `tracks` |
| `createPlaylist` | `{name}` | `Playlist` |
| `renamePlaylist` | `{id, name}` | |
| `deletePlaylist` | `{id}` | |
| `addToPlaylist`, `removeFromPlaylist` | `{id, trackIds}` | |
| `movePlaylistTrack` | `{id, from, to}` | |
| `shows` | | `[Show]` |
| `show` | `{id, offset}` | `{show, episodes, more}` |
| `stations` | | `[Station]` |
| `stationNext` | `{id}` | `[Track]` |
| `comments` | `{trackId, offset}` | `{comments, total, more}` |
| `likeComment` | `{trackId, commentId, on}` | |
| `postComment` | `{trackId, text}` | `Comment` |
| `lyrics` | `{id}` | `{lrc, translation}`, or `{lines}` with timed `words` |
| `stream` | `{id, quality}` | `{url, type, headers, size, gain, peak}`, where `type` is `mp3`, `flac`, `ogg`, `wav`, `m4a` (ALAC, FLAC or AAC-LC, whole or in fragments as a DASH stream serves it) or `aac` (AAC-LC in ADTS) |
| `remotePlay` | `{ids, start, position}` | |
| `remotePause`, `remoteResume` | | |
| `remoteSeek` | `{position}` | |
| `remoteVolume` | `{percent}` | |
| `remoteState` | | `{playing, trackId, position, duration, volume, device}` or `null` |
| `remoteDevices` | | `[{id, name, active}]` |
| `remoteUse` | `{deviceId}` | |

The shapes are in [`internal/music/music.go`](internal/music/music.go) by their JSON names. Times are in milliseconds. A `Browse` is `{title, subtitle, imageUrl, description, sections}`: with an `imageUrl`, such as a listener's avatar, it's headed round, as an artist's page is, and `description` goes under the title a line to each line. A section can hold `tracks`, `albums`, `artists`, `playlists`, `shows`, `stations`, `links` (`{title, subtitle, imageUrl, page}`), a `morePage`, and `empty`, what it says while it holds nothing. A source's first section of `tracks` leads its Home as a card of the day's songs, which opens a page of all of them, headed by the section's `pageTitle` if it has one, else its `title`, and its `subtitle` after the count of songs. A show's `publisherPage` is a `browse` page of who publishes it, which their name on the show's page opens.

An `imageUrl` can say where its size goes, with `{size}`, for an image server that makes pictures the size asked: `https://img.example.com/cover.jpg?param={size}y{size}` or `https://img.example.com/{size}/cover.jpg`. The app fills in how many pixels across it shows the picture at, 40 in a row and 600 in Now Playing, or 600 where nothing asks for a size. `%7Bsize%7D`, as JavaScript's `URL` writes it in a query, counts too. An app older than 0.1.20 fetches `{size}` as it is, so a plugin that gives it wants a `minAppVersion` of 0.1.20. Without it, give pictures at about 800 pixels if the service can, rather than as large as they were made: the app fetches and decodes the whole of each, a few megabytes for one thousands of pixels across, to show it in a row.

Of the `playlists`, those with `mine` are the listener's own, listed under My Playlists, and the rest are ones they saved. One that is `mine` and also `fixed`, such as the songs they liked, is kept by the source itself: the app doesn't offer to rename it, delete it, add songs to it, take them out or move them.

`navigation` is the plugin's sidebar, in its order. An entry opens a `browse` page of its own by `page`, or one of the app's by `builtin`: `home`, `liked`, `savedAlbums`, `stations` or `shows`, which can be given a `title`. Without `navigation`, the sidebar has an entry for each of the app's pages the plugin can do. Up to four stations show as a switch over one card, and more as a grid.

`minAppVersion` is the oldest version of MyGo Music the plugin works with. An older one won't install it, and says to update first. Versions before 0.1.8 don't read it.

### Translating a plugin

Put the translations in `locales/<language>.json` next to `plugin.json`: `locales/zh-CN.json` for Simplified Chinese, the language the app speaks besides English. Each one maps the English text to the translation:

```json
{ "Example": "示例", "API Key": "API 密钥", "From your account page": "在你的账号页面获取", "Charts": "排行榜" }
```

The app translates the plugin's `name`, its settings' `label` and `help` and its `navigation` titles with them. For what the plugin says itself, such as a page's titles or an error's message, `host.t(text)` answers the translation, or `text` when there's none, and `host.language()` the listener's language, `en` or `zh-CN`. Both follow the listener as they change it, and the page they're on loads again.

With `"playback": "stream"`, the app plays what `stream` answers. With `"playback": "remote"`, the plugin makes the sound itself, or has another program do so, and the app calls the `remote` functions and polls `remoteState`.

Throw an error with a `code` to say what's wrong: `signIn` prompts the listener to sign in, `setup` sends them to the plugin's settings, `unavailable` means this can't be played, and `unsupported` means the plugin doesn't do this. Any other error shows its message.

### Publishing a plugin

Put it in a public GitHub repository, with `plugin.json` at the top. The app takes the latest release: a `.zip` asset named for the platform, such as `plugin-darwin-arm64.zip`, or one named for none, or else the source. Without a release it takes the latest commit of the default branch. A new tag or commit is a new version, which shows as an update in the settings. An update asking for more permissions asks the listener again.

Add the topic `mygo-music-plugin` to the repository to have it listed on the [plugins page](https://mygo-music.egoist.dev/plugins).

Link to `mygo-music://install-plugin?repo=owner/repo` for an install button: it opens the app, which downloads the plugin and asks the listener before installing it. The development app (`mygo dev`) answers `mygo-music-dev://` instead.

### What a plugin can reach

A plugin has the JavaScript standard library, timers, `fetch` and its relatives, `URL`, `console` and `host`:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `host.platform`, `host.arch` | such as `darwin`, `arm64` |
| `host.dir`, `host.dataDir` | the plugin's folder, and one for its data |
| `host.storage.get(key)`, `.set(key, value)`, `.remove(key)` | JSON values that outlive the app |
| `host.setting(key)` | what the listener filled in |
| `host.t(text)`, `host.language()` | the text in the listener's language, from the plugin's `locales`, and that language: `en` or `zh-CN` |
| `host.removeDataDir(name)` | removes a folder inside `host.dataDir` |
| `host.crypto.md5(text)` | its hash, in hex |
| `host.crypto.aesEcbEncrypt(key, text)` | AES-ECB with PKCS#7 padding, in hex, for services whose requests are made that way |
| `host.openURL(url)` | opens a web page in the listener's browser |
| `host.signInPrompt({qr, text})` | what the sign-in window shows while `signIn` goes on: a QR code to scan, and what to do |
| `host.waitForRedirect({port, path, timeout, page})` | the end of a browser sign-in: listens on `127.0.0.1` and answers the query it's redirected back with. Needs the network permission |
| `host.webSignIn({url, cookiesOf, until, userAgent})` | a sign-in on the service's own page, for one that has no other way in: the app shows `url` in a window of its own, apart from every other page and forgotten after, and once the cookies named in `until` are all there, closes it and answers `{cookie}`, the Cookie header a request to `cookiesOf` would send. `cookiesOf` has to be a host the network permission reaches. `userAgent` is what the page is told it's shown in |
| `host.spawn(command, args)` | starts a program, by a path from the plugin's folder or absolute, or a name on `PATH`. Needs the process permission to name it. Returns `{pid, write(text), closeStdin(), readLine(), wait(), kill(), errorOutput()}` |

Everything else takes a permission in `plugin.json`:

- `"network": ["api.example.com", "*.example.com"]` lists the hosts `fetch` can reach, or `["*"]` for any. Without it, `fetch` reaches nothing.
- `"requestHeaders"` are headers the app sends with what it fetches itself for the plugin, its pictures (`image`) and its songs' audio (`audio`), for a service that keeps those behind its session as well as its API:

  ```json
  "requestHeaders": [
    { "hosts": ["{setting:server}"], "kinds": ["image", "audio"], "headers": { "cookie": "music-token={storage:token}" } },
    { "hosts": ["img.example.com"], "kinds": ["image"], "headers": { "referer": "https://example.com/" } }
  ]
  ```

  `hosts` are hosts or `*.domain`, which the network permission has to reach, or `{setting:key}`, the host of the server a setting names, such as `https://nas.local:5666`, while the network permission reaches it. `*` isn't one. Without `kinds`, they go with both. In `headers`, `{setting:key}` is what the listener filled in and `{storage:key}` what the plugin keeps with `host.storage`, as each is when the request goes out: a token the plugin stores anew goes with the next one, and none is kept in a URL. A header whose value isn't there yet, as before signing in, is left out. The headers a `stream` answers come first. Neither goes on to another host a request is redirected to.
- `"process": ["bin/helper-*", "ffmpeg"]` lists the programs `host.spawn` can start, for what JavaScript can't do: a path from the plugin's folder or absolute, or a name looked up on `PATH`. A path only matches a path and a name only a name, and `*` matches within one folder, as in a glob. `["*"]`, or `true`, asks for any program, which the listener is warned about. The listener has to allow it in Settings first, as a program can do anything they can. Programs end when the plugin does, and once allowed, `fetch` can reach this machine too, to talk to them. Ship one binary per platform and pick it with `host.platform` and `host.arch`.

## Credits

- [folia-major](https://github.com/chthollyphile/folia-major): the lyric stage animations

## License

AGPL-3.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

items.title: jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm
items.description: Run your own Switch games natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac: game code rewritten to ARM64, graphics direct to Metal, one app for the whole library. Bring your own games and keys. 把你自己的 Switch 游戏原生带到 iPhone / iPad / Mac。
items.readme:
**Your own Switch games, running natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac.** Game code is rewritten to native ARM64 and runs directly on the device's processor, with graphics going straight to Metal. Your whole library lives in one app, and a few clicks in the Mac or Windows launcher take a game from import to play. Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS / iPadOS 18 and later) · Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 15 and later) · Build on Mac or Windows · Android / HarmonyOS coming soon · License: Apache-2.0 · **Bring your own games** [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Download the launcher](https://jhaizhou-ops.github.io/S2Arm/) · [All releases](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/releases) · [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md)

## A native port, not an emulator The game's own ARM64 code is rewritten at build time and then runs directly on the processor in your iPhone, iPad or Mac. There is no CPU emulator in between. Graphics calls are translated straight to Metal, and system services come from a native host. That is where the speed, the low heat and the battery life come from. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#native-port) ## One app, your whole library Every game you import goes into the same S2Arm app; open it and pick what to play. The whole library takes a single App slot on your developer account, so adding a game never means installing another app or spending another signing slot. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#one-app-whole-library) ## Graphical launchers, next to zero setup There is a graphical launcher for Mac and one for Windows. On first launch the welcome page boils everything down to three steps: get this computer ready, add your keys, add your games, with a single primary button at any moment. Everything else is either bundled or fetched in one click, and you never touch a command line. After you click Build, every stage shows its progress, elapsed and remaining time, and disk use. Several games can queue up and build one after another. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#graphical-launchers)

## Let an AI drive Both the Mac and Windows launchers expose a control interface, `s2armctl`. An AI assistant can import games, build, install, follow progress and read errors, and every step shows up in the launcher window. A companion self-check, self-fix and feedback toolkit lets the AI find a problem, apply the documented fix, and, when it cannot, package a diagnostic bundle for you to file. Watch an AI diagnose and fix a real problem end to end: [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#ai-at-the-wheel) ### Have an AI do it for you Send this to your AI assistant (it needs to be able to run commands on your computer): > Please read https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/blob/main/launchers/macos/skill/s2arm-operator/SKILL.md and then help me install my Switch game on my iPhone. It moves forward with a few commands, and you can watch every step in the launcher window: ```bash /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl start # open and connect to the launcher /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl next # what to do now, who does it, and why /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl diag export ~/Desktop/S2Arm-diagnostics.zip # export a diagnostic bundle if it cannot fix a problem ``` Anything only you can do (system permission prompts, signing in with your Apple ID, tapping Trust on your phone), the AI stops and asks you to do. On Windows, use `s2armctl.cmd` in the launcher folder with the same commands; exporting a diagnostic bundle is currently Mac-only. ## Tested at scale **211** games surveyed with a **95%** first-try build success rate. **4,700+** test runs on real iOS devices and **1,000+** on macOS. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#tested-at-scale) ## Fast, smooth, and easy on the battery On a 16 GB MacBook Air (M3), from importing a game to a finished iPhone build, completely cold: | Game | Game files | Shaders | Build time | |---|---|---|---| | Diablo III | 23.5 GB | 1,222 | **6.4 min** | | Animal Crossing: New Horizons | 12.0 GB | 9,315 | **8.6 min** | | The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom | 17.5 GB | 26,999 | **34 min** | The Nintendo Switch 2 edition of *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time*, measured on an iPhone 17 Pro Max: a **full 60 fps** while the phone is cool, **37–43 fps** once sustained load has heated it up, at about **0.15 J per frame**. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#speed-and-efficiency) ## Platforms | Platform | Support | |---|---| | iPhone / iPad | iOS / iPadOS 18 and later; every game is chosen inside one app | | Mac | Apple silicon, macOS 15 and later; builds locally and plays games right on the Mac | | Windows | Graphical launcher that builds and installs games for iPhone / iPad | | Android / HarmonyOS | Coming soon | [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#platforms) ## Getting started 1. Download the Mac or Windows launcher from the [download page](https://jhaizhou-ops.github.io/S2Arm/) and open it. Building for iPhone on a Mac needs the free Xcode from the App Store, signed in with your Apple ID; the launcher walks you through it. 2. Import your own keys and games. Put the base game, updates and DLC in one folder and import them together. 3. Choose iPhone / iPad or this Mac, then click Build. 4. Follow the launcher to sign and install with your own Apple ID (the Windows launcher ships with the Impactor signing tool), open S2Arm, and pick a game from the library. Back up your saves before updating the app. The release uses the new app identifier `io.s2arm.*`, which the system treats as a new app: saves from the beta builds do not carry over automatically. ## Honest boundaries S2Arm runs 64-bit (AArch64) games. Apple silicon cannot execute 32-bit ARM code, so 32-bit games are outside what S2Arm supports. Confirmed so far: Ni no Kuni: Wrath of the White Witch, Goat Simulator, New Super Mario Bros. U Deluxe and Monster Hunter XX. Minecraft: Story Mode, which needs a 36-bit address space, is outside it as well. The full list with versions is on the [evidence page](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#unsupported-games). ## Development [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [AI collaboration policy](LLM_POLICY.md) · [Diagnosis and root-fix skills for AI](skills/) · [Report a problem](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/issues) · [Third-party licenses](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md) ## Thanks S2Arm stands on the shoulders of its community. - **Co-developers**: thank you to everyone who has opened a pull request or issue in this project. Your code, device testing and bug reports shaped S2Arm (in order of first contribution): [@biglawine](https://github.com/biglawine), [@yyan160](https://github.com/yyan160), [@DanielZhangyc](https://github.com/DanielZhangyc), [@vickwv](https://github.com/vickwv), [@Xc1Ym](https://github.com/Xc1Ym), [@fjack](https://github.com/fjack), [@ha7rock](https://github.com/ha7rock), [@yourmoonlight](https://github.com/yourmoonlight), [@qidian99](https://github.com/qidian99), [@n06ody](https://github.com/n06ody), [@YTwsy](https://github.com/YTwsy), [@wdjwxh](https://github.com/wdjwxh), [@realskyrin](https://github.com/realskyrin), [@wwmogu](https://github.com/wwmogu), [@quancunlau](https://github.com/quancunlau), [@moongrant](https://github.com/moongrant), [@imyinyx](https://github.com/imyinyx), [@s-leeq](https://github.com/s-leeq), [@Zhangbu](https://github.com/Zhangbu), [@retX0](https://github.com/retX0), [@zh0ngtian](https://github.com/zh0ngtian), [@fengbird](https://github.com/fengbird), [@zsakvo](https://github.com/zsakvo), [@1500256797](https://github.com/1500256797), [@BossaMelon](https://github.com/BossaMelon), [@GayoZhao](https://github.com/GayoZhao), [@sovaly](https://github.com/sovaly), [@ruterfu](https://github.com/ruterfu), [@fyn1320068837-source](https://github.com/fyn1320068837-source), [@InTheManXG](https://github.com/InTheManXG). - **Ryujinx** (Ryujinx Team and Contributors, MIT): upstream for system services and shader translation; S2Arm's compatibility layer is built on it. - **[NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple)** (LNPANDY, MIT): upstream of the launcher interface. - **[nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)** (seedds, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 seedds): the original work behind the direct graphics layer that connects game graphics straight to Metal. That generous release is what made the direct path possible. - **[d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile)** (MIT): pioneered this technical path, bringing your own Switch game natively to iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android and HarmonyOS for the first time. - **Impactor** (Samara M, MIT) and **apple-codesign** (MPL-2.0): signing and installing from Windows. - **LNPANDY** and the original authors and contributors of the iOS library shell: the shell and its RomFS archive subsystem. - **ns2pro-bridge** (DanielZhangyc, MIT), **MacNativeGames** (MIT), **LumaDock** (MIT), **deko3d** (fincs, zlib), **nvn.h** (h1k421, MIT), **bcdec** (Sergii Kudlai, MIT / Unlicense), **LibHac** (Alex Barney, MIT) and **hactool** (SciresM, ISC), **SPIRV-Cross** and **Vulkan-Headers** (The Khronos Group), **SMAA** (Jorge Jimenez et al., MIT), the **Mesa** tessellator (Microsoft, MIT), **Capstone**, **LZ4**, **.NET**, **libvpx**, **libopus**, **dav1d**, and the **Noto** fonts. Versions, full license texts and what each component does are in [NOTICE](NOTICE) and the [third-party license list](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md). ## Star History ## License and legal S2Arm is open source under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). The project ships no games and no keys; obtain your own game files legally. S2Arm is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, and game titles and trademarks belong to their respective owners.

items.title: sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp
items.description: Ocarina of Time running natively on Windows, no emulator. Built on your PC from your own copy. No game files included.
items.readme:
# Ocarina Recomp

[Read in English](README.en.md)

**Ocarina rodando nativo no Windows, sem emulador.**

O código do jogo é traduzido para C e compilado como um programa do Windows. Os gráficos do Switch 2 são convertidos para Vulkan. Tudo isso acontece **no seu PC, a partir do seu próprio arquivo do jogo**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Este repositório **não contém o jogo, keys nem executável**, e não explica como obtê-los. Você precisa da sua própria cópia. O que a instalação gera (o `ocarina.exe`, o código gerado, o cache de shaders e os saves) sai do seu jogo: **não compartilhe**.

## Estado do projeto

Experimental. Só foi testado em **um PC** (Ryzen 9 9950X3D, RTX 5090), na região do início do jogo.

| O quê | Situação |
|---|---|
| Abertura e jogo novo, até a Árvore Deku | ✅ Funciona |
| Vilarejo Kokiri: árvores, plantas, casas, luz | ✅ Funciona |
| Som, controle, saves e vídeos | ✅ Funciona |
| Desempenho na RTX 5090 | ✅ Cerca de 59 fps parado, 51 a 55 fps caminhando |
| Travadinhas ao entrar em áreas novas | ⚠️ Ainda acontecem, principalmente na primeira vez |
| Tocar a ocarina | ❓ Correção aplicada, ainda sem teste em jogo |
| Hyrule Field e o resto do jogo | ❓ Ainda não testados |
| Placas AMD e Intel | ❓ Nunca testadas |

## Como compilar

O jogo não vem pronto: ele é compilado no seu PC, a partir da sua cópia. Escolha um destes três jeitos.

**1. Com o instalador em ZIP, o mais fácil:** não instala nada no Windows e não pede administrador.

1. Baixe o **`Ocarina-Setup-...-windows.zip`** da [página de versões](https://github.com/sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp/releases/latest).
2. **Extraia o ZIP inteiro** para uma pasta e abra o `Instalar-Ocarina.exe` que está dentro dela.
3. O executável não tem assinatura digital, então o Windows pode avisar. Clique em **Mais informações** e depois em **Executar assim mesmo**.
4. Na janela, escolha o `.nup` do seu jogo (ou uma pasta com `exefs` e `romfs`) e clique em **Instalar**.
5. No fim, clique em **Jogar**, ou use o atalho **Ocarina Recomp** na Área de Trabalho.

Para desinstalar, apague a pasta de instalação. Prefere conferir antes? O executável só abre o script `instalador\Instalar-Ocarina.ps1`, que está ao lado dele no ZIP e pode ser lido em qualquer editor. O [código do executável](instalador/launcher.c) tem poucas linhas. Alguns antivírus reclamam de programas novos sem assinatura e de scripts do PowerShell: é um alarme possível, e o código está todo aqui para quem quiser conferir. A página de versões traz o SHA-256 do arquivo.

> [!NOTE]
> A etapa "Preparar os arquivos do jogo" é lenta, principalmente em HD: enquanto o relógio da janela andar, está funcionando.

**2. Com os scripts, que você pode ler antes de rodar** (instale antes as ferramentas do passo 1 do [guia](docs/compilar-manual.md)):

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp C:\OcarinaRecomp
cd C:\OcarinaRecomp
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\verificar.ps1 -Jogo "C:\caminho\seu-jogo.nup"
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\compilar.ps1 -Simular -Jogo "C:\caminho\seu-jogo.nup"
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\compilar.ps1 -Jogo "C:\caminho\seu-jogo.nup"
```

1. O `verificar.ps1` só olha e diz o que falta. Ele não altera nada.
2. O `compilar.ps1 -Simular` mostra todos os comandos sem executar nenhum.
3. O `compilar.ps1` executa esses comandos, mostra cada um e pergunta antes de cada etapa. Se parar, rode de novo: ele continua de onde parou.

`-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` vale só para esse comando e não muda a configuração do Windows.

**3. Totalmente à mão:** siga o **[passo a passo para compilar](docs/compilar-manual.md)**.

**No Linux:** o `compilar.sh` faz os mesmos passos e o `jogar/jogar-ocarina.sh` abre o jogo. Os pacotes e o estado do
port estão em [docs/building.md](docs/building.md#linux-in-progress).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp
cd ocarina-recomp
./compilar.sh --jogo /caminho/seu-jogo.nup
./jogar/jogar-ocarina.sh
```

### Trazer o save de um emulador

O save do Lichii, do Eden e de emuladores parecidos funciona aqui. No fim da instalação, clique em **Importar save de emulador**, ou rode depois:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File jogar\importar-save.ps1
```

Ele acha o save sozinho ou pergunta a pasta, guarda uma cópia do seu save atual e não altera o emulador.

### Idioma

O jogo escolhe o idioma pelo do Windows, inclusive português do Brasil. Para trocar, aperte **F1** e vá em **Jogo → Idioma**.

### O que isto faz no seu PC

- O instalador em ZIP e os scripts não pedem administrador. Só as ferramentas dos jeitos 2 e 3 podem pedir, e é você quem as instala.
- Escreve só dentro da pasta do projeto, e nunca altera o seu arquivo do jogo.
- Baixa os pacotes Python (`tools\requirements-build.txt`) e .NET do tradutor de shaders e, se o executável do jogo estiver comprimido, o [zbic](https://github.com/kinnay/zbic).
- Para desinstalar, apague a pasta do projeto. As ferramentas do passo 1 saem pelo painel de aplicativos do Windows.

Leva de 30 minutos a 2 horas, e você pode usar o PC enquanto isso. Para atualizar, rode de novo o instalador ou veja o fim do guia.

> [!NOTE]
> Na primeira vez que abrir o jogo, **a vegetação pode levar alguns minutos para aparecer**, enquanto os shaders compilam em segundo plano. Melhora nas próximas vezes.

### Do que você precisa

- Windows 10 ou 11 de 64 bits, com processador compatível com AVX2.
- Placa de vídeo com Vulkan 1.3 e mesh shaders, com o driver atualizado. Recomendamos NVIDIA.
- Recomendamos 16 GB de RAM ou mais. Com menos, nunca testamos: a compilação ou o jogo podem falhar.
- Com 16 GB de RAM, aumente o arquivo de paginação do Windows antes de jogar (inicial 16384 MB, máximo 32768 MB): na primeira vez o jogo pode chegar a uns 24 GB de memória, e o Windows fecha o jogo se passar do limite. O instalador avisa quando o limite é baixo.
- 40 GB livres com o instalador em ZIP. Nos outros dois jeitos, 60 GB, mais uns 15 GB no disco C: para as ferramentas.
- Internet durante a instalação.
- **Sua cópia do jogo na versão 1.1.1.** Outras versões não funcionam.

### Se algo der errado

| Problema | O que fazer |
|---|---|
| "Este jogo não é a versão 1.1.1" | Confira se escolheu o jogo certo e atualizado |
| O jogo abre e fecha | Atualize o driver da placa de vídeo e veja o arquivo `ultima-partida-erros.log` na pasta de instalação |
| O jogo fechou no meio | O log de cada partida fica guardado em `logs\` (as últimas 10). `jogar\medir-partida.ps1` mostra o crash e o desempenho. |
| Travadinhas na primeira vez | É normal: os shaders estão sendo preparados. Melhora quando você passa de novo pelo mesmo lugar |

Se continuar, [abra uma issue](https://github.com/sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp/issues) com a mensagem de erro e o modelo da sua placa de vídeo. Nunca envie arquivos do jogo.

### Controles

Use um controle ou teclado e mouse. **F1** ou **Esc** abre o menu de opções, **F11** alterna a tela cheia e **F10** mostra o fps. A lista completa está em [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md).

## Como funciona

1. `recomp/gen.py` traduz o código ARM64 do jogo para C.
2. `tools/build_game.py` compila esse C junto com o `runtime/`, que faz o papel do sistema do console.
3. `runtime/` converte as chamadas gráficas NVN 2 para Vulkan.
4. Os shaders Ampere do Switch 2 são rebaixados para Maxwell (`lower_to_maxwell.h`) e traduzidos para SPIR-V por um Ryujinx com patches (`tools/xlate/patches`).

## Quer ajudar?

Leia o **[guia de contribuição](CONTRIBUTING.md)**. Testar em outras placas de vídeo e relatar o resultado já ajuda muito.

## Créditos

Projeto mantido por **Miojo** ([sostenesfreitas](https://github.com/sostenesfreitas)). Dizem que ele deixou um recado escondido no instalador e outro dentro do jogo. 🍜

Este projeto existe graças ao trabalho de muita gente:

- **[Lucas-blip-png/dkb-pc-recomp](https://github.com/Lucas-blip-png/dkb-pc-recomp)** e TotK Recomp: a base deste projeto, cujo histórico continua preservado aqui.
- **[seedds/nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)**: referência de como o jogo usa task e mesh, e correção do microfone.
- **[zortos293/Lichii](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii)** e Eglantine/Eden: o rebaixamento de shaders Ampere e a referência para comparar os draws.
- **[Ryujinx](https://github.com/Ryujinx/Ryujinx)**: o tradutor de shaders.
- **[kinnay/zbic](https://github.com/kinnay/zbic)**: descompressão do executável, baixada durante a instalação.

A lista completa está em [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Licença

items.title: Th0rgal/satmux
items.description: Accelerate high-latency GEO inflight Wi-Fi via warm BBR TCP multiplexing + 1-RTT Ground-TLS + zlib (zero dependencies)
items.readme:
# satmux

TCP multiplexer and `1-RTT` HTTP/TLS relay for geostationary (GEO) inflight Wi-Fi (Inmarsat GX, Viasat, Panasonic, SITA). Pure Python 3 stdlib, zero external dependencies.

Measured inflight over Inmarsat GX Ka-band (`~620 ms` RTT, SITA `AS206433` Amsterdam ground station):

```text
  ORIGIN (6× PARALLEL)  RAW CABIN WI-FI (:443)    1-RTT BBR + ZLIB MUX    SPEEDUP
  ────────────────────  ────────────────────────  ──────────────────────  ─────────
  GitHub Repo           ████████████    TIMEOUT  ███░░░░░░░░░    4.66s  FIXED ✓
  GitHub API            ████████████  TCP RESET  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.66s  FIXED ✓
  Hacker News           ████████████    TIMEOUT  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.28s  FIXED ✓
  MDN Docs              ████████░░░░     12.01s  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.30s     5.2×
  Cloudflare            ██░░░░░░░░░░      2.97s  █░░░░░░░░░░░    1.40s     2.1×
  PyPI JSON API         █████░░░░░░░      7.09s  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.64s     2.7×
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  6-Origin Burst:    19.13s (3/6 failed)  →  5.35s (0/6 failed)   [3.6× faster · -76% TTFB]
```

## Problem

Non-Starlink inflight Wi-Fi usually breaks on three things unrelated to raw bandwidth:

1. **Onboard `:443` middleboxes and DNS interception.** Cabin gateways intercept `:53` DNS and run a transparent `:443` split-TCP proxy (PEP) whose state table drops connections under load (`Connection reset by peer` / TLS timeouts on `github.com`, `api.github.com`, package registries). Non-443 TCP ports pass through untouched.
2. **Handshake round-trips (`~620 ms` per GEO hop).** Every new origin normally pays multiple satellite round-trips (DNS + TCP + TLS) before transferring payload bytes.
3. **Cubic congestion collapse.** Cabin Wi-Fi packet loss causes standard TCP to halve `cwnd` repeatedly, leaving most of your per-seat token-bucket cap unused.

## How it works

```text
Direct (:443):
  laptop ──▶ cabin DNS + :443 PEP ══(3–4 GEO RTTs)══▶ ground ──▶ origin  (frequent TCP resets)

satmux (:8444):
  laptop ══(12 persistent TCP :8444 BBR + zlib pipes)══▶ ground VM ──(2 ms)──▶ origin
```

- **Persistent non-443 carrier pool (`:8444`):** Keeps 12 pre-warmed TCP connections open to a Linux VM near the satellite ground station, bypassing the cabin `:443` proxy and onboard DNS. Streams are scheduled onto the carrier with the lowest recent byte load so idle browser keepalives do not cause head-of-line queueing.
- **0-RTT stream open (`127.0.0.1:1080` SOCKS5 / `127.0.0.1:8080` HTTP CONNECT):** Returns `OK` locally in `<1 ms` and sends `FT_OPEN` + TLS `ClientHello` in the same TCP burst, saving one full satellite RTT while preserving end-to-end TLS from the laptop.
- **1-RTT ground fetch (`127.0.0.1:8081`):** Sends an encrypted (`BLAKE2b-512` stream + `HMAC-SHA256`) request frame over a warm carrier. The ground VM performs DNS, verified TLS 1.3, and HTTP redirects on fiber (`~2–5 ms`) and compresses plaintext responses with `zlib` before crossing the satellite link.
- **`git` and `gh` CLI routing:** Go binaries such as `gh` ignore macOS `scutil` proxies. `satmux` exposes a `0600` local Unix socket (`/tmp/satmux-gh-tls.sock`) wired to `gh`'s `http_unix_socket` that wraps requests in verified end-to-end TLS on the laptop and tunnels them over SOCKS5, fixing already-running coding agents without restarting them.
- **BBR + `MSS 1280`:** Ground-to-cabin sockets enable `TCP_CONGESTION=bbr` and `TCP_MAXSEG=1280`.

## Limits

- **Latency floor (`~580–650 ms`):** Speed-of-light propagation to geostationary orbit (`35,786 km`) does not change; `satmux` removes extra round-trips, not the physical RTT of one hop.
- **Per-seat shaper (`~4–5 Mbps` typical):** Cabin routers police total bandwidth per client lease. Compressible traffic (HTML, JSON, code, APIs) exceeds that rate in effective throughput via `zlib`; already-compressed binaries (`.mp4`, `.zip`) stay bounded by the seat cap (though BBR + parallel `satmux-get` keep throughput near the ceiling).
- **Single paid session:** Uses your authenticated cabin Wi-Fi lease; it does not bypass captive portals.

## Setup

### 1. Ground VM

Rent a small Linux VM (`$0.01–$0.03/h`, Python 3.9+, open TCP port `8444`) close to where the satellite downlinks to fiber. Check `curl ipinfo.io` on raw cabin Wi-Fi first to see the egress country/ASN:

- **Emirates / Middle East & European flights (Inmarsat GX / SITA `AS206433`):** Amsterdam, Frankfurt, or Hetzner EU (downlink lands in the Netherlands).
- **North America:** `us-east` or `us-west`.
- **Asia-Pacific:** Singapore or Tokyo.

Pause UDP VPNs (Tailscale/WireGuard) inflight—blocked UDP retry traffic competes for cabin airtime.

### 2. Run

With a coding agent:

> Spin up a temporary Ubuntu VM near my current satellite egress IP, start `https://github.com/Th0rgal/satmux` on port `8444`, connect the local 12-carrier client, enable `bin/satmux-macos on`, and run `bin/satmux-bench`.

Or manually:

```bash
# 1. Laptop: generate PSK
git clone https://github.com/Th0rgal/satmux.git && cd satmux
openssl rand -hex 32 > mux.psk && chmod 600 mux.psk

# 2. Ground VM: start server
scp satmux.py mux.psk root@<SERVER_IP>:/root/
ssh root@<SERVER_IP> 'nohup env SATMUX_PSK=$(cat /root/mux.psk) python3 /root/satmux.py server --port 8444 >/var/log/satmux.log 2>&1 &'

# 3. Laptop: start client + enable macOS / git / gh routing
SATMUX_PSK=$(cat mux.psk) python3 satmux.py client --host <SERVER_IP> --port 8444 --carriers 12 &
./bin/satmux-macos on <SERVER_IP>
```

Benchmark or run parallel range downloads:

```bash
./bin/satmux-bench
./bin/satmux-get https://example.com/archive.tar.gz
```

### 3. Teardown after landing

```bash
./bin/satmux-macos off
```

Restores macOS Wi-Fi proxy settings, `~/.gitconfig`, `gh` `http_unix_socket`, and `launchctl` env vars, then destroy the temporary VM.

横屏 · 左字右图
 竖屏 · 手机阅读优化
[看完整故事和12页动作](examples/storybooks/tea-party/README.md) · [什么图适合做](styles/compact-storybook/STYLE.md) · [稳定版 Skill](skills/compact-storybook/SKILL.md) 可以直接说： > 使用 $pixel-gif-sticker-pack，选“紧凑动态绘本”，把这个故事做成6帧固定画面小动画，先给一页看看。 ## 制作说明 外观、动作和用途分别选择：像素可以做轻动效，也可以做完整动作；光栅是变画方法，漫画印刷是设计语言。风格入口把可用组合整理给你，不表示所有素材和动作都已验证。 每次交付核对实际 GIF、数量、循环时长和画面；“高清”“帧数够了”不能替代人物稳定与审美检查。已认可、待确认和弃用的版本分开保留。 ## 开源许可 制作脚本与 Skill 文档采用 [MIT](LICENSE)。动态海报的角色与参考设计语言不随代码转授商业权利，见[案例说明](examples/dynamic-posters/p5-integrated/README.md)。电子光栅卡中的角色 IP、网络照片与他人插画不随代码一并授予 MIT 权利，出处及使用边界见[案例来源说明](examples/lenticular-cards/README.md)。 第三方配乐和字体按各自许可使用；面包店案例的来源与署名见 [CREDITS](examples/brand-films/manman-bakery/CREDITS.md)。
